# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

Should it be considered less worthy of a hearing, or less instructive as a reflection of ancient opinions, than any other religious work? Other such works are also "compilations from old texts" or oral traditions from the same or even a later period. If that were the case, we would have to reject the *Quran* <note>original: "Kurân"</note>—written three centuries later—and label it "apocryphal" <term>a work of doubtful authenticity</term>, even though we know it emerged fully formed—like the goddess Minerva from the head of Jupiter—directly from the mind of the Arabian prophet Muhammad. We would also have to dismiss all the information we can gather from the *Talmud*, which, in its current form, was also compiled from older materials and dates no earlier than the ninth century C.E. <note>Common Era</note>.

This unusual "Bible" of the Chaldean Adept <term>a master of esoteric knowledge</term> and the various critiques of it (such as those in Chwolsohn’s translation) are mentioned here because they have a significant impact on much of this current work. Aside from the arguments of Ernest Renan—a man who challenged established beliefs on principle and was sharply described by Jules Lemaître as "the Paganini of nothingness" <note>original: "*le Paganini du néant*"</note>—the worst fault found with the work seems to be that the text <note>original: "*apocryphon*"</note> claims to have been communicated as a *revelation* to an Adept by the "idol of the Moon," who supposedly received it from "Saturn." 

Consequently, critics naturally dismiss it as "a total fairy tale." There is only one answer to this: it is no more a fairy tale than the *Bible*, and if one is dismissed, the other must follow. Even the method of seeking divine guidance through the "idol of the Moon" is the same as the practice used by David, Saul, and the High Priests of the Jewish Tabernacle using the Teraphim <term>small household idols or figurines used for divination in ancient Israel</term>.

*Nabathean Agriculture* is indeed a compilation. It is not a fake text <note>original: "*apocryphon*"</note>, but rather a restatement of the principles of the Secret Doctrine. It uses the external <term>exoteric</term> symbols of Chaldean culture to "disguise" these teachings, just as the *Books of Hermes* and the *Puranas* were similar attempts by the Egyptians and Hindus. The work was as well known in ancient times as it was during the Middle Ages. The philosopher Maimonides mentions it and refers to this Chaldean-Arabic manuscript several times. He calls the Nabatheans "Sabæans" or "star-worshippers" (the name of their fellow believers). However, he fails to recognize that the word "Nabathean" is a corrupted form of the mystical name for the group dedicated to Nebo, the God of *Secret Wisdom*. This connection clearly suggests that the Nabatheans were an occult brotherhood.* The Nabatheans who, according to the Persian...

# NEBO, THE GOD OF WISDOM.

The Yezidis, who originally came to Syria from Basra <note>original: "Busrah"</note>, were the degenerate members of that brotherhood; nonetheless, even at that late date, their religion was purely Kabbalistic <note>original: "kabalistic," referring to Jewish mystical traditions</note>.* Nebo is the deity associated with the planet Mercury, and Mercury is the God of Wisdom—also known as Hermes or Budha <note>In Hindu astrology, Budha is the planet Mercury, not to be confused with Gautama Buddha</note>—whom the Jews called *Kokab* <note>original: ככב; Hebrew for "star" or "planet," specifically Mercury</note>, "the Lord on high, the aspiring," and the Greeks called *Nabo* <note>original: Ναβώ</note>; hence the name Nabatheans. Despite the fact that Maimonides <note>A famous 12th-century Jewish philosopher</note> calls their doctrines "heathenish foolishness" and their ancient literature "the offspring of the Sabaeans" <note>original: "*Sabæorum fœtum*"</note>, he still places their work on *agriculture*—the "Bible" of the initiate Qû-tâmy—in the highest rank of ancient literature; and the scholar Abarbanel praises it in unmeasured terms. John Spencer,† quoting Abarbanel, speaks of it as that "most excellent oriental work," adding that by "Nabatheans," one must understand the Sabaeans, the Chaldeans, and the Egyptians—in short, all those nations against whom the laws of Moses were most severely enacted.

Nebo, the oldest God of Wisdom in Babylonia and Mesopotamia, was identical to the Hindu Budha and the Hermes-Mercury of the Greeks. The only difference lies in a slight change in the gender of the parents. Just as Budha was the son of Soma (the Moon) in India and the wife of Brihaspati (Jupiter), so Nebo was the son of Zarpanitu (the Moon goddess) and of Merodach <note>also known as Marduk</note>, who became Jupiter after having been a Sun-god. As the planet Mercury, Nebo was the "overseer" among the seven gods of the planets; and as the personification of Secret Wisdom, he was *Nabin*, a seer and a prophet <note>The Hebrew word for prophet, *Nabi*, is derived from this root</note>. The biblical account has Moses die and disappear on the mountain sacred to Nebo. This shows him to have been an Initiate and a priest of that God under another name; for this God of Wisdom was the great Creative Deity and was worshipped as such. This worship occurred not only at Borsippa in his magnificent Temple, or "Planet-tower," but he was likewise adored by the Moabites, the Canaanites, the Assyrians, and throughout the whole of Palestine. Why, then, would the Israelites not have worshipped him as well? "The planetary temple of Babylon" had its "Holy of Holies" within the shrine of Nebo, the Prophet-God of Wisdom. We are told in the Hibbert Lectures:

> The ancient Babylonians had an intercessor between men and the gods . . . and Nebo was the "proclaimer" or "prophet," as he made known the desire of his father Merodach.‡

Nebo is a Creator, like Budha, of the Fourth and also of the Fifth Race <term>In Theosophy, the Fourth and Fifth "Root Races" refer to the Atlanteans and the current human race, respectively</term>. For the former starts a new race of Adepts <term>highly evolved spiritual masters</term>, and the latter starts the Solar-Lunar Dynasty, or the men of these particular Races and Rounds. Both are—

### THE KABBALISTIC FOUR ADAMS

...the admirably clear description of these found in Isaac Myer’s *Qabbalah*. He lists only four Adams—undoubtedly because of the Kings of Edom <note>In Kabbalah, the "Kings of Edom" represent earlier, unbalanced worlds that were destroyed before the current creation</note>—and adds:

> The fourth Adam . . . was clothed with skin, flesh, nerves, and so on. This corresponds to the lower animal soul <note>original: *Nephash*</note> and physical body <note>original: *Guff*</note> united. He possesses the animal power of reproduction and the continuation of the species.*

This represents the *human Root-Race* <note>In Theosophy, a Root-Race is a major stage in human evolution; the "fourth" refers to the Atlantean period</note>.

It is at this exact point that modern Kabbalists—led into error by generations of Christian mystics who tampered with Kabbalistic records whenever possible—diverge from the Occultists in their interpretations, mistaking later developments for the original ideas. The original *Kabbalah* was entirely metaphysical and was not concerned with animal or earthly sexes; the later *Kabbalah* has smothered the divine ideal under a heavy emphasis on sexual <note>original: "phallic"</note> elements. The Kabbalists say: "God made man male and female." The author of the *Qabbalah* states:

> Among the Kabbalists, the necessity for continued creation and existence is called the Balance.†

Because they lack this "Balance"—which is connected with the "Place" <note>original: *Maqom*; a Hebrew term for the Divine, but also used here to refer to the source of physical life</note>—even the First Race is not recognized by the "Sons of the Fifth Adam" <note>the current human race</note>, as we have seen. From the highest Heavenly Man—the Upper Adam who is "male-female" or androgynous—down to the "Adam of dust," these personified symbols are all connected with sex and procreation in the Kabbalah.

For Eastern Occultists, it is the complete opposite. They view sexual relations as a form of "Karma" <note>The law of cause and effect</note> pertaining only to the worldly existence of a person dominated by Illusion <note>original: Maya</note>. It is something to be set aside the moment a person becomes "wise." They considered it a very fortunate circumstance if the *Guru* <note>spiritual teacher</note> found in his pupil a natural inclination for the pure life of celibate study <note>original: *Brahmâchârya*</note>. To them, their dual symbols were merely poetic imagery for the sublime relationship between creative cosmic forces. This ideal conception shines like a golden ray from every idol—no matter how coarse or grotesque—in the crowded galleries of the dark temples <note>original: *fanes*</note> of India and other ancient homelands of these faiths.

This will be demonstrated in the following section.

## SECTION III.
### THE “HOLY OF HOLIES.” ITS DEGRADATION.
---
The "Holy of Holies" <note>original: *Sanctum Sanctorum*</note> of the ancients, also called the innermost sanctuary <note>original: *Adytum*</note>—the recess at the west end of the temple which was enclosed on three sides by blank walls and had its only opening or door covered with a curtain—was common to all ancient nations.

A great difference is now found between the secret meaning of this symbolic place as given in the inner teachings <note>original: Esotericism</note> of the Pagans and in those of the later Jews, though its symbolism was originally identical among all ancient races and nations. The non-Jewish nations <note>original: Gentiles</note> placed in the innermost sanctuary a stone coffin <note>original: *sarcophagus*</note> or a tomb <note>original: *taphos*</note> containing the Solar God to whom the temple was dedicated; as pantheists <note>those who believe the divine is present in all things</note>, they held this in the greatest reverence. They regarded it, in its inner meaning, as the symbol of resurrection—cosmic, solar (daily), and human. It encompassed the wide range of periodic and precise "Manvantaras" <note>In Hindu and Theosophical thought, a long period of activity or manifestation of the universe</note>, or the reawakenings of the Universe <note>original: Kosmos</note>, Earth, and humanity to new existences. The Sun was the most poetic and grandest symbol of such heavenly cycles, while human reincarnation represented these cycles on Earth.

The Jews—whose literalness, if judged by the surface meaning, was as practical and crude in the days of Moses as it is now\*—completed a national and priestly <note>original: levitical</note> political system during their separation from the Gods of their Pagan neighbors. They did this by presenting their "Holy of Holies" as the most solemn sign of their monotheism <note>the belief in one God</note> for the public, while seeing it only as a universal fertility symbol <note>original: phallic symbol</note> in their secret teachings. While the Kabbalists <note>Jewish mystics</note> knew only *Ain Suph* <note>The Infinite or Boundless God</note> and the "Gods" of the Mysteries, the Levites <note>the Jewish priestly class</note> had no tomb and no God in their innermost sanctuary except the "Sacred" Ark of the Covenant—their "Holy of Holies."

\* But this was not the case in reality, as their prophets show. It is the later Rabbis and the Talmudic scheme that drained all spirituality from their symbols, leaving their Scriptures as a dead shell from which the soul has departed.

The Ark is the boat-shaped <note>original: "navi-form"</note> *Argha* <note>a ceremonial vessel in Hindu ritual, symbolizing the female principle or the womb of nature</note> of the Mysteries. Precisely; and the Jewish Ark of the Covenant had *exactly the same meaning*; with the added detail that, instead of a beautiful and pure stone coffin <note>original: "sarcophagus"</note> (the symbol of the Womb of Nature and Resurrection) as in the Holy of Holies <note>original: "Sanctum Sanctorum"</note> of the Pagans, they made the Ark even more literal in its design. Furthermore, the meaning of this reproductive symbol was reinforced by the four mystical letters of Jehovah’s name, namely, IHVH (יהוה); *Jod* (י) meaning the male organ <note>original: "membrum virile"</note>; *Hé* (ה), the womb; *Vau* (ו), a crook, a hook, or a nail; and *Hé* (ה) again, meaning "an opening." The whole forms the perfect two-sexed <note>original: "bisexual"</note> emblem or symbol of I-E-H-O-V-A-H, the male and female symbol.

Iacchus <note>a name for Dionysus or Bacchus used in the Eleusinian Mysteries</note> is again Iao or Jehovah; and Baal or Adon, like Bacchus, was a phallic God <note>a deity associated with reproductive power</note>.

# WHO WAS ABRAXAS?

The numerical or Kabbalistic <note>Referring to the Kabbalah, a system of Jewish mysticism where letters have numerical values</note> value of the name Abraxas directly refers to the Persian title of the god Mithras, the Ruler of the year. ### THE EVIL SPIRIT: WHO, AND WHAT?

Our current disagreement is strictly with Theology. The Church demands belief in a personal God and a personal Devil, whereas Occultism demonstrates why such beliefs are mistaken. For Pantheists <note>Those who believe the universe and God are one and the same</note> and Occultists—just as much as for Pessimists—"Nature" appears to be nothing more than "a beautiful mother, but stone cold." However, this is only true regarding external, physical Nature. Both groups agree that, to a casual observer, she seems like nothing more than a massive slaughterhouse where the butchers eventually become victims, and the victims take their turn as executioners. 

It is natural for those with a pessimistic outlook who are not initiated into these mysteries to see Nature's many shortcomings and failures—especially her self-consuming <note>original: "autophagous"</note> tendencies—and conclude that this is the best evidence that there is no hidden Deity <note>original: "Deity in abscondito"</note> within Nature, nor anything divine in her. Similarly, it is natural for Materialists and physicists to assume that everything results from blind force and chance, where the strongest survive even more often than the most well-adapted <note>original: "fittest"</note>. 

However, Occultists view the Great Mother <note>A symbolic name for Nature or the divine feminine principle of creation</note> differently. They see physical Nature as a collection of various illusions created by our deceptive senses. They recognize that every instance of pain and suffering is merely the necessary labor pains of ongoing creation—a series of stages leading toward a constant state of improvement. This progress is visible in the silent influence of never-failing Karma <note>The law of cause and effect</note>, also known as "Abstract Nature." Occultists say that we must view the Great Mother in this light. Woe to those who live without suffering. Stagnation and death are the future for everything that exists without change. # THE "MONKEY OF GOD."

Is it not only those who have learned the deceptive value of earthly hopes and the illusive charms of external nature who are destined to solve the great problems of life, pain, and death?

If our modern philosophers—following in the footsteps of medieval scholars—have borrowed more than one fundamental idea from antiquity, theologians have constructed their God and his archangels, their Satan and his angels, along with the <term>Logos</term> <note>The Word or divine reason</note> and his attendants, entirely from the cast of characters <note>original: "dramatis personæ"</note> of the ancient pagan pantheons. They would have been welcome to use these characters if they had not cunningly distorted the original figures, perverted the philosophical meaning, and taken advantage of the ignorance of Christendom. This ignorance was the result of long ages of mental sleep, during which humanity was permitted to think only through the Church <note>original: "by proxy"</note>. In doing so, they tossed every symbol into the most hopeless confusion. One of their most harmful achievements in this effort was the transformation of the divine counterpart <note>original: "Alter Ego"</note> into the grotesque Satan of their theology.

As the entire philosophy of the problem of evil depends on correctly understanding the nature of the *Inner Being* of Nature and Man—the divine within the animal—the accuracy of the entire system presented in these pages regarding the pinnacle <note>original: "crown piece"</note> of evolution, Man, depends on this as well. Therefore, we cannot take enough precautions against theological deceptions. When the saintly Augustine and the fiery Tertullian call the Devil the "monkey of God," we can attribute it to the ignorance of the era in which they lived. It is more difficult to excuse our modern writers for the same mistake.

# THE GENESIS OF THE DEVIL.

The "Spirit of God"—which, for the older Babylonians as for the <term>Akkadians</term> <note>An ancient Mesopotamian people who preceded the Babylonians</note>, lived in the "Sea of Space"—was originally a cosmic force. Toward the era described by <term>Berosus</term> <note>A Babylonian writer and priest from the 3rd century BCE</note>, this Sea became the "Visible Waters" on the face of the Earth. These waters were the crystalline home of the Great Mother (the mother of <term>Ea</term> <note>The Babylonian god of wisdom and water</note> and all the Gods). Later, this figure became the great Dragon <term>Tiamat</term> <note>A primordial goddess of the ocean, often depicted as a sea serpent or dragon representing chaos</note>, the Sea Serpent. The final stage of this myth's development was the great struggle of the god <term>Bel</term> <note>A title meaning "Lord," often applied to the Babylonian god Marduk</note> with the Dragon—who was eventually transformed into the Devil!

Where did the Christian idea that God cursed the Devil come from? The God of the Jews, whoever he was, actually forbids cursing Satan. <term>Philo Judæus</term> <note>A Hellenistic Jewish philosopher from Alexandria</note> and <term>Josephus</term> <note>A first-century Romano-Jewish historian</note> both state that the *Law* (the *Pentateuch* and the *Talmud*) consistently forbids one from cursing the Adversary <note>Satan</note>, and also forbids cursing the Gods of the <term>Gentiles</term> <note>Non-Jewish people or nations</note>. "You shall not revile the gods," said the God of Moses,\* for it is God who "has divided [them] among all nations";† and those who speak evil of "Dignities" <note>In this context, high-ranking spiritual beings or deities</note> are called "filthy dreamers" by the Apostle Jude.

For even Michael the Archangel . . . dared not bring a reviling accusation against him [the Devil], but said, "The Lord rebuke you."‡

Finally, the same sentiment is repeated in the *Talmud*:§

> Satan appeared one day to a man who used to curse him daily, and said to him: "Why do you do this?" Consider that God *himself* would not curse me, but merely said: "The Lord rebuke you, Satan."||

This piece of Talmudic information shows plainly (**a**) that Saint Michael is called "God" in the Talmud, while someone else is called the "Lord," and (**b**) that Satan is a God of whom even the "Lord" is afraid. Everything we read in the *Zohar* and other <term>Kabalistic</term> <note>Relating to Jewish mysticism</note> works concerning Satan shows plainly that this "personage" is simply the personification of abstract Evil. This evil is the weapon of <term>Karmic Law</term> <note>The spiritual principle of cause and effect</note> and <term>Karma</term>. It represents our human nature and man himself, as it is said that "Satan is always near and inextricably interwoven with man." It is only a question of whether that Power is latent or active within us.

It is a well-known fact—at least to learned <term>Symbologists</term> <note>Those who study the meaning and history of symbols</note>—that in every great religion of antiquity, it is the <term>Logos Demiurge</term> <note>The "Word" or "Creator" figure who fashions the physical world</note>—the Second Logos, or the first emanation from the Universal Mind, <term>Mahat</term> <note>A Sanskrit term for the "Great" cosmic intelligence</note>—who is made to set the tone, so to speak, for the relationship between the Individual and the Personality in the subsequent plan of existence...

# THE SONS OF ETERNITY.

Speculations have gradually acquired the importance of dogma and inspired tradition. Everyone sought to explain the verse about the seven-headed dragon with his ten horns and seven crowns, whose tail “drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth,” and whose place, along with that of his Angels, “was found no more in heaven.” What the seven heads of the Dragon (the symbol of a Cycle) mean, and its *five* wicked kings as well, may be learned in the Addenda which close Part III of this Volume.

From Isaac Newton to Bossuet <note>Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet (1627–1704), a prominent French bishop and theologian</note>, speculations were incessantly produced by Christian thinkers regarding these obscure verses. Bossuet says:

> The star that falls is the heresiarch <note>a leader of a heretical sect</note> Theodosius. . . . The clouds of smoke are the heresies of the Montanists <note>an early Christian movement that emphasized new prophetic revelations</note>. . . . The third part of the stars are the martyrs, and especially the doctors of divinity.

Bossuet ought to have known, however, that the events described in the Book of *Revelation* were not original. As has been shown, they can be found in other and earlier Pagan traditions. There were no scholastics nor Montanists during the Vedic times <note>the ancient period of Indian history when the Vedas were composed</note>, nor in the even earlier history of China. But Christian Theology had to be protected and saved at any cost.

This is only natural. But why should truth be sacrificed in order to protect the laborious theories <note>original: "lucubrations"</note> of Christian theologians from destruction?

The “Prince of this air” <note>original: *princeps aeris hujus*</note> mentioned by St. Paul is not the Devil, but the effects of the Astral Light, as Éliphas Lévi <note>a famous 19th-century French occultist</note> correctly explains. The Devil is not the “God of *this period*,” as Lévi says; rather, this "Devil" represents the Deity of every age and period since humanity appeared on Earth, during which Matter—in its countless forms and states—has had to fight for its temporary existence against other disintegrating forces.

The “Dragon” is simply the symbol of the Cycle and of the “Sons of Manvantaric <term>Manvantara</term> <note>a vast period of time in Hindu cosmology during which a universe exists and is active</note> Eternity,” who descended to Earth during a certain epoch of its formative period. The “clouds of smoke” are geological phenomena. The “third part of the stars of heaven” cast down to the Earth refers to the Divine Monads—the Spirits of the Stars in Astrology—that orbit our globe. These are the *human Egos* destined to perform the entire Cycle of Incarnations. 

The phrase, “who walks around the earth” <note>original: *qui circumambulat terram*</note>, however, is again attributed to the Devil in Theology; the mythical Father of Evil is said to “fall like lightning.” Unfortunately for this interpretation, the “Son of Man,” or Christ, is also expected to descend to Earth “as the lightning comes out of the East,”* according to the personal testimony of Jesus—just in the same manner.

the same shape and under the same symbol as Satan, who is seen to fall "as lightning . . . from heaven." <note>Luke 10:18</note> We must look to the East for the origin of all these metaphors and figures of speech, which are distinctly Oriental in character. In all ancient theories of the universe <term>cosmogonies</term>, light emerges from darkness. In Egypt, as elsewhere, darkness was considered "the source of all things." Consequently, Pymander <note>original: "Pymander," referring to the *Poimandres*, a fundamental text of Hermeticism representing "Divine Thought" or "The Shepherd of Men"</note>, the "Divine Thought," emerges as light from the darkness. Behemoth <margin>The Protestant Bible innocently defines Behemoth as "the elephant as some think"; see the marginal note for Job 40:15 in the Authorized Version <note>The King James Version</note>.</margin> is the principle of darkness, or Satan, in Roman Catholic theology, and yet the Book of Job says of him that Behemoth is "the chief [principle] of the ways of God"—"Behemoth is the beginning of the ways of the Lord!" <note>original Latin: "*Principium viarum Domini Behemoth!*" from Job 40:19</note>

Consistency does not seem to be a highly valued virtue in any part of what is called "Divine Revelation"—at least, not as interpreted by theologians.

The Egyptians and the Chaldeans traced the birth of their divine dynasties to that period when the creative Earth was in her final labor pains, giving birth to her prehistoric mountain ranges (which have since disappeared), her seas, and her continents. Her surface was covered with "deep darkness," and within that [secondary] Chaos lay the "principle of all things" that developed on the globe later on. Our geologists have now confirmed that such a terrestrial conflagration <note>a massive fire or period of intense heat</note> occurred in the early geological periods, several hundred million years ago. <margin>Astronomy, however, knows nothing of stars that have disappeared, except in terms of visibility; they never cease to exist, at least not since the science of astronomy began. Temporary stars are merely variable stars, and it is believed that even the "new" stars observed by Kepler and Tycho Brahe may still be visible.</margin> As for the tradition itself, every country and nation had it, each expressed in its own national form.

It is not only Egypt, Greece, Scandinavia, or Mexico that had their Typhon, Python, Loki, and their "fallen" demon, but China as well. The Chinese have an entire literature on this subject. It is said that because a proud spirit—who claimed he was Ti <note>a Chinese term for a supreme deity or "Heaven"</note> himself—rebelled against Ti, seven choirs of celestial spirits were exiled to Earth. This "brought a change to all of Nature, with Heaven itself bending down and uniting with Earth."

In the *I Ching* <note>original: *Y-King*</note>, one reads:

> The flying dragon, proud and rebellious, suffers now, and his pride is punished; he thought he would reign in Heaven, but he reigns only on the Earth.

# THE SHADOWS OF THE SHADOWS.

Again, the *Spring and Autumn Annals* <note>original: *Tchoon-Tsieoo*, a classic Chinese historical text</note> says allegorically:

> One night the stars stopped shining in the darkness and deserted it, falling down like rain upon the Earth, *where they are now hidden.*

These stars are the <term>Monads</term> <note>individual sparks of divine consciousness or souls</note>.

Chinese <term>cosmogonies</term> <note>stories of the origin of the universe</note> have their “Lord of the Flame” and their “Celestial Virgin,” with little “Spirits to help and serve her; and great Spirits to fight those who are the enemies of other Gods.” But all of this does not prove that these allegories are merely previews or *prophetic writings* that all point toward Christian theology.

The best proof one can offer to Christian theologians that the <term>esoteric</term> <note>hidden or inner</note> statements in the *Bible*—in both Testaments—express the same idea as our ancient teachings is found in the *Zohar* <note>the foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>. This teaching suggests that the “Fall of the Angels” referred simply to the incarnation of angels “who had broken through the Seven Circles.” Now, the <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>Jewish mystical tradition</note> of Simeon Ben Iochai is the soul and essence of this allegorical narrative, just as the later *Christian Kabbalah* is the “darkly disguised” Mosaic Pentateuch <note>the first five books of the Bible</note>. It says (in the Agrippa manuscripts):

> The wisdom of the Kabbalah rests in the science of equilibrium and harmony.
> 
> Forces that manifest without having been first balanced <note>differentiated</note> perish in space.
> 
> Thus perished the first Kings [the Divine Dynasties] of the Ancient World, the *self-produced Princes of Giants*. They fell like rootless trees and were seen no more; *for they were the Shadow of the Shadow* [that is, the <term>Chhaya</term> <note>shadow or astral image</note> of the Shadowy <term>Pitris</term> <note>the ancestral spirits or progenitors of humanity</note>].<margin>This refers to the "Kings of Edom." <note>In Kabbalistic tradition, the Kings of Edom represent early, unbalanced attempts at creation that failed because they could not contain the divine light.</note></margin>
> 
> But those who came after them, who shot down like falling stars and were enshrined in the Shadows, have prevailed to this day [the <term>Dhyanis</term> <note>celestial or meditative beings</note> who, by incarnating in those “empty Shadows,” began the era of humanity].

Every sentence in the ancient stories of the universe's origin reveals the identity of these ideas to anyone who can read between the lines, even though they are dressed in different clothing.

The first lesson taught in <term>Esoteric Philosophy</term> is that the Incognizable Cause <note>The Absolute or ultimate reality that cannot be fully known</note> does not undergo evolution, whether consciously or unconsciously. Instead, it periodically shows *different aspects* of itself to the perception of *finite* minds. Now, the Collective Mind—the Universal Mind—is composed of various and countless hosts of creative powers. However infinite this mind may seem during the time the universe exists, it is still finite when compared to the Unborn and Undecaying Space in its supreme, essential aspect. That which is finite cannot be perfect. Therefore, there are inferior...

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

There are beings among those Hosts, but there have never been any "Devils" or "disobedient Angels" for the simple reason that all are governed by Law. The <term>Asuras</term> <note>original: "Asuras," a class of spiritual beings in Hindu mythology who were later depicted as demons, but here viewed as powerful creative forces</note> (call them by any other name you wish) who took physical form followed a law in this process that was as unrelenting as any other law of nature. They had appeared before the <term>Pitris</term> <note>original: "Pitris," the ancestral spirits or "fathers" of humanity</note>, and as Time (in Space) proceeds in cycles, their turn had come to manifest—this is the source of many allegories. The name "Asura" was first used by the <term>Brahmins</term> <note>the priestly caste of India</note> indiscriminately to describe those who opposed their superficial rituals and sacrifices, such as the great Asura called Asurendra. The idea of the "Demon" as an opponent and adversary can probably be traced back to those ancient times.

The Hebrew <term>Elohim</term> <note>a name for God or gods in the Hebrew Bible</note>—who are called "God" in modern translations—are the ones who create "Light," and they are identical to the ancient <term>Aryan</term> <note>referring to the ancient Indo-Iranian peoples</note> Asuras. They are also referred to as the "Sons of Darkness" as a logical and philosophical contrast to the Light that is Unchanging and Eternal. The earliest <term>Zoroastrians</term> <note>followers of the ancient Persian religion founded by Zoroaster</note> did not believe that Evil or Darkness existed forever alongside Good or Light, and they provide the same interpretation. <term>Ahriman</term> <note>the personification of darkness or evil in Zoroastrianism</note> is the manifested *Shadow* of <term>Ahura Mazda</term> <note>the supreme creator deity</note>. Ahura Mazda himself came from <term>Zeruana Akerne</term> <note>original: "Zeruâna Âkerne," the personification of "Boundless Time"</note>, the "Boundless Circle of Time" or the Unknown Cause. They say of the latter:

> Its glory is too high, and its light is too brilliant for either the human mind or the mortal eye to understand and see.

Its first output is **Eternal Light**. Because this light was previously hidden in Darkness, it was called to reveal itself, and thus **Ormazd** <note>another name for Ahura Mazda</note>, the "King of Life," was formed. He is the "First-born" within Boundless Time, but—just like his own spiritual blueprint—he has lived within Darkness *from all Eternity*. The six **Amshaspands** <note>the "Bounteous Immortals," a class of six divine beings in Zoroastrianism</note>—seven including himself as their leader—are the primary **Spiritual Angels and Men** who collectively form his **Logos** <note>the divine word or creative reason</note>. The Zoroastrian Amshaspands also create the World in six "Days" or periods and rest on the seventh. However, in the **Esoteric Philosophy**, that *seventh* day is actually the first period or "Day"—the so-called **Primary Creation** in ancient Indian origin-stories. It is that intermediate **Aeon** <note>original: "Æon," a long period of time or a divine power</note> that serves as the **Prologue to Creation**. It stands on the border between the Uncreated Eternal Cause and the produced, finite effects—a state of emerging activity and energy that serves as the first expression of the Eternal, Unchanging Stillness. In the book of *Genesis*—where no deep metaphysical thought was applied, but only an extraordinary cleverness to hide the hidden truth—Creation begins at the third stage of development. "God" or the Elohim are the "Seven Regents" mentioned in the <term>Pymander</term> <note>original: "Pymander," the *Poimandres*, a foundational text of the Hermetic tradition</note>. They are identical to all other creator-beings.

# WHO THE <term>ÂDITYAS</term> ARE.

But even in the Book of *Genesis*, that period is hinted at by the abruptness of the description and the "Darkness" that was on the face of the Deep. The <term>Elohim</term> <note>original: "Elohim," a Hebrew name for God, plural in form, interpreted here as a collective of divine builders.</note> are shown to "create"—that is to say, to build or to produce—the two Heavens or the "double" Heaven (*not* Heaven and Earth). In plain words, this means they separated the upper manifested (Angelic) Heaven, or plane of consciousness, from the lower or terrestrial plane. They separated the (to us) Eternal and Unchanging <term>Æons</term> <note>original: "Æons," divine emanations or powers in Gnostic thought.</note> from those periods that exist in space, time, and duration; they separated Heaven from Earth, the Unknown from the Known—at least to the <term>profane</term> <note>original: "profane," referring here to the uninitiated or those without secret knowledge.</note>. Such is the meaning of the sentence in the *Pymander* <note>a foundational text of Hermeticism, an ancient philosophical and religious tradition</note>, which says that:

> Thought, the *divine*, which is Light and Life [<term>Zeruâna Âkerne</term> <note>original: "Zeruâna Âkerne," a Zoroastrian term for Boundless Time.</note>] produced through its Word, or first aspect, the other, *operating Thought*. This being the God of Spirit and Fire, it constructed Seven Regents who enclose the World of Senses, named "Fatal Destiny," within their circle.

The latter term refers to <term>Karma</term> <note>the law of cause and effect.</note>. The "Seven Circles" are the seven planets and planes, as well as the seven Invisible Spirits in the Angelic Spheres, whose visible symbols are the seven planets*, the seven <term>Rishis</term> <note>original: "Rishis," the seven ancient seers of Indian tradition, often associated with the stars of the Big Dipper.</note> of the Great Bear, and other symbols. As was said of the Âdityas by the scholar Roth:

> They are neither sun, nor moon, nor stars, nor dawn, but the eternal sustainers of this luminous life which exists, as it were, behind all these phenomena.

It is they—the "Seven Hosts"—who, having "considered the plan of the operator within their Father [Divine Thought]," as the *Pymander* says, *desired to operate* (or build the world with its creatures) likewise. Because they were born *within* the "Sphere of Operation"—the manifesting Universe—this follows <term>Manvantaric Law</term> <note>the cosmic law governing the long cycles of the universe's existence.</note>. And now comes the second portion of the passage, or rather of two passages merged into one to conceal the full meaning. Those who were born within the Sphere of Operation were "the brothers who loved *him* well." The latter—the "him"—were the Primordial Angels: the <term>Asuras</term>, <term>Ahriman</term> <note>the destructive spirit in Zoroastrianism, here viewed as a necessary force of nature.</note>, the Elohim, or "Sons of God," of whom Satan was one. These are all those Spiritual Beings who were called the "Angels of Darkness" because that Darkness is actually absolute Light—a fact now neglected, if not entirely forgotten, in modern Theology. Nevertheless, the spirituality of those much-abused "Sons of Light" (which is Darkness) must evidently be as much greater than the next order of Angels as the ethereal nature of those Angels is greater than the density of the human body. The former are the "First-born," and are therefore so near to the boundaries of—

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

Pure, still Spirit was considered to be merely "privations"—in the <term>Aristotelian</term> <note>Aristotle used "privation" to describe the absence of a quality or form that should naturally be present.</note> sense—the <term>Ferouers</term> <note>original: "Ferouers" (Fravashi); in Zoroastrianism, these are the pre-existing, spiritual archetypes or guardian souls of all beings.</note> or the ideal types of those who followed. They could not create material, *physical* things; and, therefore, in the course of time, they were said to have "refused" to create as "commanded" by "God"—or, in other words, to have "rebelled."

Perhaps this is justified by the principle of the *scientific theory* that teaches us about the effect of two sound waves of equal length meeting:

> If the two sounds are of the same intensity, their coincidence produces a sound four times the intensity of either, while their interference produces *absolute silence*.

While explaining some of the "heresies" of his day, <term>Justin Martyr</term> <note>original: "Justin Martyr" (c. 100–165 AD), an early Christian apologist who sought to find common ground between Christianity and Greek philosophy.</note> shows the identity of all the world’s religions at their starting points. The *first Beginning* invariably opens with the *Unknown* and *Passive Deity*, from which flows a certain Active Power or Virtue—the Mystery that is sometimes called Wisdom, sometimes the Son, and very often God, Angel, Lord, and <term>Logos</term> <note>original: "Logos," a Greek term meaning "Word" or "Reason," representing the divine creative principle.</note>.* This last term is sometimes applied to the very first emanation, but in several systems, it proceeds from the first <term>Androgyne</term> <note>A being possessing both male and female characteristics; here representing a dual creative force.</note> or "Double Ray" produced at the beginning by the Unseen. <term>Philo</term> <note>original: "Philo Judæus" (c. 20 BC – 50 AD), a Hellenistic Jewish philosopher who used allegory to fuse Greek philosophy with Jewish scripture.</note> depicts this Wisdom as both male and female. But though its first manifestation had a beginning—for it proceeded from <term>Oulom</term>† <note>original: "Oulom" (Hebrew: Olam), often meaning eternity, the world, or a long duration of time.</note> (<term>Aeon</term>, Time), the highest of the <term>Aeons</term> <note>In Gnosticism, these are the various emanations or powers that come from the ultimate God.</note> when sent out from the Father—it had remained with the Father *before all creations*, for it is part of him.‡ Therefore, Philo Judæus calls <term>Adam Kadmon</term> <note>In Kabbalah, the "Primordial Man," the first spiritual reflection of the Divine.</note> by the name "Mind"—the <term>Ennoia</term> <note>A Gnostic term for "Thought" or "Intent."</note> of <term>Bythos</term> <note>A Gnostic term for "the Deep" or the primal "Abyss."</note> in the Gnostic System. "The Mind, let it be named Adam."§

As the old <term>Magian</term> <note>Referring to the Magi, the priestly caste of ancient Persia and the followers of Zoroastrianism.</note> books explain it, the whole event becomes clear. A thing can only exist through its opposite—as <term>Hegel</term> <note>Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel (1770–1831), a German philosopher known for his dialectical method where a thesis and antithesis lead to a synthesis.</note> teaches us; and only a little philosophy and spirituality are needed to comprehend the origin of the later dogma, which is so truly satanic and infernal in its cold and cruel wickedness. The Magians accounted for the Origin of Evil in their <term>exoteric</term> <note>Teachings intended for the public or the uninitiated, as opposed to "esoteric" secret teachings.</note> teachings in this way: "Light can produce nothing but Light, and can never be the origin of Evil." How then was Evil produced, since there was nothing equal to or like the Light in its production? Light, they say, produced several Beings, all of them spiritual, luminous, and powerful. But a Great One (the "Great <term>Asura</term>," <note>In later Hindu texts, Asuras are demons, but in the oldest Vedas, they were powerful deities; here equated with Ahriman or Lucifer.</note> Ahriman, Lucifer, etc.) had an evil thought, contrary to the Light. He doubted, and by that doubt, he became dark.

# THE "ZOHAR" <note>original: "Zohar"; the "Book of Radiance," a foundational work of Jewish Kabbalah (mysticism) likely written or compiled in the 13th century.</note> ON THE "FALLEN ONES."

This is slightly closer to the truth, but it still misses the mark. There was no "evil thought" that originated the opposing Power. Instead, it was simply Thought in itself <note>original: "per se"</note>—something which, being capable of thinking and containing design and purpose, is therefore finite. Consequently, it must naturally find itself in opposition to pure Quiescence, which is the natural state of absolute Spirituality and Perfection. It was simply the Law of Evolution asserting itself. The progress of Mental Unfolding, once separated from Spirit, became involved and entangled with Matter, into which it is irresistibly drawn. Ideas, by their very nature and essence, are conceptions related to objects—whether those objects are real or imaginary. Therefore, ideas are opposed to Absolute Thought—that Unknowable All. Regarding this "All," Mr. Spencer <note>Herbert Spencer (1820–1903), a Victorian philosopher famous for applying evolutionary theory to philosophy and psychology.</note> claims that nothing can be said, except that "it has no natural connection <note>original: "kinship of nature"</note> with Evolution"*—which it certainly does not.†

The *Book of Radiance* <note>original: "Zohar"</note> describes this very suggestively. When the "Holy One" (the Divine Reason <note>original: "Logos"</note>) desired to create man, he called the *highest* Host of Angels and told them what he wanted. However, they doubted the wisdom of this desire and answered: "Man will not last one night in his glory"—for which they were destroyed <note>original: "burnt (annihilated?)"</note> by the "Holy" Lord. Then he called another, lower group of angels, and said the same. They also argued against the "Holy One": "What is the good of Man?" they asked. Still, the Divine Powers <note>original: "Elohim"</note> created Man. When Man sinned, the angel groups of Uzza and Azael <note>In Jewish lore, these are leaders of the "fallen angels" who descended to earth.</note> came and mocked God: "Here is the Son of Man that you have made," they said. "Look, he has sinned!" Then the Holy One replied: "If you had lived among them [Men], you would have been worse than they." Then he threw them from their high position in Heaven down to the Earth; and "they were changed [into Men] and sinned with the women of the earth."‡ This is quite clear. No mention is made in *Genesis* (chapter 6) of these "Sons of God" receiving punishment. The only reference to it in the Bible is in the book of *Jude*:

> And the angels who did not keep their first status but left their own home, he has kept in everlasting chains under darkness until the judgment of the great day.§

-># THE SECRET DOCTRINE.<-

And this simply means that the "Angels," who are destined to take on physical form <note>original: "doomed to incarnation"</note>, are bound by the chains of flesh and matter. They remain in the darkness of ignorance until the "Great Day," which always arrives after the Seventh Round, following the completion of the "Week"—on the Seventh Sabbath, or within the post-cosmic state of liberation <note>original: "Post-Manvantaric Nirvâna." A "Manvantara" is a vast period of cosmic activity; Nirvana here refers to the rest period between such cycles.</note>.

How truly esoteric and consistent with the Secret Doctrine the *Pymander* <note>The *Pymander* (or *Poimandres*) is a foundational text of Hermeticism, traditionally attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, representing the "Divine Mind."</note> is can be seen from its original and primitive translations in Latin and Greek. On the other hand, we can see how it was later distorted by European Christians through the comments and unintentional admissions made by De St. Marc in his 1578 preface and letter to the Bishop of Aire. In those writings, the entire process of transforming an Egyptian, pantheistic <note>Pantheism: the belief that the universe itself is identical with divinity.</note> text into a mystical Roman Catholic treatise is laid out. We can see how the *Pymander* has become what it is today. Yet, even in St. Marc's translation, traces of the true *Pymander*—the "Universal Thought" or "Mind"—can still be found. The following is a translation of an old French version (the original 16th-century French is provided in the footnote*):

> Seven men [principles] were generated in Man. . . . The nature of the harmony of the Seven of the Father and of the Spirit. Nature . . . produced seven men in accordance with the natures of the Seven Spirits . . . having within them, potentially, both sexes.

Metaphysically, the Father and the Son represent the "Universal Mind" and the "Periodical Universe"; the "Angel" and the "Man." This entity is the Son and the Father at the same time. In the *Pymander*, this is the **active** Idea and the **passive** Thought that generates it. It is the fundamental keynote in Nature that gives birth to the seven notes—the sevenfold scale of Creative Forces—and to the seven prismatic colors, all born from the one White Ray, or Light, which is itself generated in Darkness.

## THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

What can be the meaning of this last sentence if it is not a narrative of the fate of the Atlanteans? Again, the phrase "Your heart was lifted up because of your beauty," <note>original: Ezekiel 28:17</note> may refer to the "Heavenly Man" in the *Pymander* <note>A foundational Hermetic text attributed to Hermes Trismegistus</note>, or to the Fallen Angels, who are accused of having fallen through pride because of the great beauty and wisdom that became their lot. There is no metaphor here, except perhaps in the preconceived ideas of our theologians. These verses relate to the past and belong more to the knowledge acquired during the mysteries of initiation <note>Secret religious rites of the ancient world where sacred knowledge was revealed</note> than to retrospective clairvoyance! The voice says again:

> You have been in Eden, the garden of God [in the *Satya Yuga* <note>original: the first "Golden Age" in Hindu cosmology</note>]; every precious stone was your covering: . . . the workmanship of your tambourines <note>original: "tabrets"</note> and your pipes was prepared in you on the day you were created. You are the anointed cherub; . . . you have walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire. . . . You were perfect in your ways from the day that you were created, until iniquity was found in you. Therefore I will cast you . . . out of the mountain of God, and . . . destroy you. <note>original: Ezekiel 28:13-16</note>

The "Mountain of God" means the "Mountain of the Gods" or Meru <note>The sacred mountain at the center of the universe in Hindu and Buddhist cosmology</note>, whose representative in the Fourth Race <note>In Theosophy, the Fourth Root Race refers to the Atlanteans</note> was Mount Atlas. This mountain was the *last form of one of the divine Titans*, so high in those days that the ancients believed the heavens rested on its top. Did not Atlas assist the giants in their war against the gods, according to the mythographer Hyginus? Another version shows the *fable* arising from the fondness of Atlas—the son of Iapetus and Clymene—for astronomy, and from his dwelling for that reason on the highest mountain peaks. 

The truth is that Atlas, the "Mountain of the Gods," and also the hero of that name, are the esoteric <note>hidden or inner</note> symbols of the Fourth Race. His seven daughters, the Atlantides, are the symbols of its seven sub-races. Mount Atlas, according to all the legends, was three times as high as it is now, for it has sunk during two different time periods. It is of volcanic origin, and therefore the voice within Ezekiel says:

> Therefore I will bring forth a fire from the midst of you; it shall devour you. <note>original: Ezekiel 28:18</note>

Surely this does not mean—as seems to be the case from the translated texts—that this fire was to be brought from the midst of the Prince of Tyre <note>original: "Tyrus"</note> or his people. Instead, it refers to Mount Atlas, symbolizing the proud race that was learned in magic and advanced in arts and civilization, whose last remnant was destroyed almost at the foot of the range of those once-gigantic mountains.

Truly, "you shall be a terror, and never shall you be anymore." <note>original: Ezekiel 28:19</note>

# VARIOUS NAMES FOR INITIATES.

As the very name of that Race <note>The Fourth Root Race, or the Atlanteans</note> and its fate has now been erased from human memory, bear in mind that almost every ancient king and priest was an <term>Initiate</term> <note>A person who has been admitted into secret religious or philosophical knowledge</note>. From toward the close of the Fourth Race, there had been a feud between the Initiates of the Right-Hand Path <note>Those practicing "white magic" or altruistic spiritual paths</note> and those of the Left-Hand Path <note>Those practicing "black magic" or selfish spiritual paths</note>. Finally, the Garden of Eden is referred to by other figures besides the Jews of the Adamic Race, since even Pharaoh is compared to the fairest tree of Eden by this same prophet Ezekiel, who shows:

> All the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon . . . were comforted in the lower regions <note>original: "nether parts"</note> of the earth. [For] they also went down into the abyss <note>original: "hell"</note> with him [Pharaoh]*—unto the lower regions, which are in fact the bottom of the ocean, whose floor gaped wide to devour the lands of the Atlanteans and the people themselves. 

If one bears all this in mind and compares the various accounts, then one will find that chapters 28 and 31 of Ezekiel do not relate to Babylon, Assyria, or even to Egypt. None of these nations were destroyed in such a way; they simply fell into ruins on the *surface* of the earth, not *beneath* it. Instead, these chapters refer to Atlantis and most of its nations. The reader will see that the “Garden of Eden” of the Initiates was no myth, but a physical location now submerged. The truth will become clear, and he will appreciate the true <term>Esoteric</term> <note>Knowledge intended for a small, specialized group</note> value of sentences such as these: “You have been in Eden; . . . you were upon the holy mountain of God”†—for every nation had, and many still have, *holy* mountains. Some were Himalayan peaks, others were Mount Parnassus and Mount Sinai. They were all places of Initiation and the homes of the leaders of the communities of ancient and even modern <term>Adepts</term> <note>Highly skilled masters of esoteric wisdom</note>. And again:

> Behold, the Assyrian [why not the Atlantean Initiate?] was a cedar in Lebanon; . . . his height was exalted above all the trees. . . . The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him: . . . so that all the trees of Eden . . . envied him.‡

Throughout all of Asia Minor, the Initiates were called the “Trees of Righteousness” and the “Cedars of Lebanon,” as were some kings of Israel. The great Adepts in India were also called this, though specifically the Adepts of the Left-Hand Path. When the *Vishnu Purana* <note>An ancient Hindu religious text</note> narrates that “the world was overrun with trees” while the Prachetasas <note>In Hindu mythology, ten brothers who were sages and princes</note>—who “passed 10,000 years of austerity in the vast ocean”—were absorbed in their devotions, the allegory relates to the Atlanteans and the Adepts of the early Fifth Race.

In other words, in its higher aspect, the mind is attracted toward <term>Buddhi</term> <note>The higher spiritual mind or intuitive wisdom</note>, while in its lower aspect, it descends into and listens to the voice of its animal soul.

The true narrative—the one that provides the full <term>Esoteric</term> <note>Hidden or inner spiritual meaning</note> meaning—is contained in the Secret Books, but the author has not had access to those.

However, the episode of the Târaka War found in the <term>exoteric</term> <note>Publicly available or outer teachings</note> works, along with some Esoteric Commentaries, may perhaps offer a clue. In every *Purâna* <note>A category of ancient Indian texts containing myths, history, and philosophy</note>, the event is described with various differences that highlight its symbolic character.

In the mythology of the earliest <term>Vedic Aryans</term> <note>The Indo-Aryan people of ancient India who composed the Vedas</note>, as well as in later <term>Pauranic</term> <note>Related to the Purânas</note> narratives, mention is made of Budha, the "Wise," one "learned in the Secret Wisdom." In his <term>euhemerization</term> <note>The interpretation of myths as being based on real historical people who were later deified</note>, he represents the planet Mercury. The *Hindu Classical Dictionary* credits Budha with being the author of a hymn in the *Rig Veda*. Therefore, he can by no means be "a later invention of the Brahmins," but is a very ancient personification indeed.

It is by inquiring into his genealogy—or rather, his <term>theogony</term> <note>The study of the origins and descent of a group of gods</note>—that the following facts are disclosed. As a myth, he is the son of Târâ (the wife of Brihaspati, the "gold-colored" one) and Soma (the male Moon). In a manner similar to the Trojan prince Paris, Soma carries this new "Helen" of the Hindu celestial kingdom away from her husband. This causes great strife and a *war* in <term>Svarga</term> <note>Heaven or the celestial realm</note>.

The episode triggers a battle between the Gods and the <term>Asuras</term> <note>A class of divine or semi-divine beings in Hindu mythology, often depicted in opposition to the Devas (gods)</note>. King Soma finds allies in Ushanas (representing the planet Venus), the leader of the <term>Danavas</term> <note>A race of mythological giants or demons</note>. The Gods are led by Indra and Rudra, who side with Brihaspati. Brihaspati is helped by Shankara (Shiva), who, having had Brihaspati's father, Angiras, as his <term>Guru</term> <note>A spiritual teacher or guide</note>, befriends the son.

In this story, Indra is the Indian prototype of Michael, the Chief Commander <note>original Greek: "Archistrategus"</note> and the slayer of the "Dragon's" Angels—since one of Indra's names is Jishnu, "leader of the celestial host." Both fight, just as some Titans did against other Titans in defense of vengeful Gods. One party fights in defense of the Thundering Jupiter <note>original Latin: "Jupiter tonans"</note>—and interestingly, in India, Brihaspati is associated with the planet Jupiter. The other party fights in support of the ever-thundering Rudra. During this war, Indra is deserted by his bodyguards, the Storm-Gods (Maruts). The story is very suggestive in some of its details.

Let us examine some of them and seek to discover their meaning.

### THE WAR OF THE TITANS.

The "War in Heaven" refers to several different events occurring on various levels of existence. The first is a strictly astronomical and cosmic reality related to the origins of the universe <note>original: "Cosmogony"</note>. John Bentley believed that for the Hindus, the "War in Heaven" was merely a symbolic figure referring to their calculations of vast time periods.*

He thinks this served as the original model for Western nations to build their "War of the Titans" upon. The author is not entirely wrong, but neither is he quite right. While the celestial <note>original: "sidereal"</note> model does indeed refer to a period before the current world-cycle <note>original: "pre-manvantaric"</note> and is based on the knowledge that Aryan Initiates claim to have regarding the entire plan and progress of cosmic development,† the War of the Titans is actually a legendary and mythological version of a real war. This conflict took place in the Himalayan region of Kailasa (a type of "Heaven") rather than in the depths of outer space. It is the record of the terrible struggle between the "Sons of God" and the "Sons of the Shadow" during the transition between the Fourth and Fifth Root-Races <note>In this context, the Fourth Race refers to the inhabitants of Atlantis, and the Fifth refers to modern humanity</note>. All later national traditions on this subject were built upon these two events, which were blended together through legends taken from public <note>original: "exoteric"</note> accounts of the war waged by the Asuras <note>Spiritual beings often later depicted as demons, but originally meaning "divine"</note> against the Gods.

From an inner, spiritual perspective <note>original: "Esoterically"</note>, the Asuras—who were later transformed into evil spirits and lesser gods eternally at war with the *Great Deities*—are actually the Gods of Secret Wisdom. In the most ancient parts of the *Rig Veda* <note>The oldest of the Hindu scriptures</note>, they are described as spiritual and divine beings. The term *Asura* was used for the Supreme Spirit and is the same as the great *Ahura* of the Zoroastrians.‡ There was a time when the Gods Indra <note>God of the sky and storms</note>, Agni <note>God of fire</note>, and Varuna <note>God of cosmic order</note> themselves were classified as Asuras.

-># THE SECRET DOCTRINE.<-

In the *Taittirîya Brâhmana* <note>A sacred commentary on the Vedas</note>, the Breath (*Asu*) of Brahmâ-Prajâpati became alive, and from that Breath, he created the *Asuras*. Later on, after the War, the Asuras are called the enemies of the Gods; thus they became the “*A-suras*”—the initial *a* being a negative prefix meaning “*No-Gods*”—while the “Gods” are referred to as *Suras*. This connects the Asuras and their “Hosts” (listed further below) with the “Fallen Angels” of the Christian Church. This hierarchy of spiritual beings is found in every national mythology <note>original: "Pantheon"</note>, from the Zoroastrian religion to Chinese traditions. They are the sons of the primeval Creative Breath at the beginning of every new Great Age <note>original: "Mahâ Kalpa"</note> or cosmic cycle <note>original: "Manvantara"</note>, holding the same rank as the angels who remained “faithful.” These were the *allies* of Soma (the source of inner wisdom <note>original: "Esoteric Wisdom"</note>) against Brihaspati (who represents ritualistic or ceremonial worship). Clearly, they have been demoted over time into opposing powers or “demons” by those who favored formal ritual, simply because they rebelled against hypocrisy, fake worship, and a literal, soulless adherence to religious rules <note>original: "dead-letter form"</note>.

In the early *Veda*, Indra is the highest God of the cosmic Heaven, the appropriate home for an external and personal God; no outward form of worship can ever rise higher than this level.

# SARPAS—SERPENTS—NÂGAS

In mythology, they are semi-divine beings with human faces and the tails of dragons. They are, therefore, undeniably the same as the Jewish **Seraphim** <note>original: "Seraphim (compare Serapis, Sarpa, Serpent)"</note>; the singular form is *Saraph*, meaning "burning" or "fiery." Christian and Jewish studies of angels <note>original: "angelology"</note> distinguish between the Seraphim and the **Cherubim** (or Cherubs), who rank second in order. However, from the perspective of inner wisdom and the Kabbalah <note>original: "Esoterically, and kabalistically"</note>, they are identical. "Cherubim" is simply the name for the images or likenesses of any of the divisions of the heavenly armies <note>original: "celestial Hosts"</note>.

Now, as stated before, "Dragons" and "**Nâgas**" <note>Ancient Sanskrit term for serpent-beings, often symbolizing wisdom</note> were the names given to the hermit-initiates because of their great wisdom and spirituality, and because they lived in caves. Thus, when the prophet Ezekiel* applies the description "Cherub" to the King of Tyre and tells him that by his wisdom and his understanding **there is no secret that can be hidden from him**, he is signaling to the student of the occult that he is a "Prophet"—perhaps still a follower of outer, public worship <note>original: "exoteric worship"</note>—who rages against an Initiate of a different school of thought. He is not attacking an imaginary Lucifer, a fallen angel from the stars or from the Garden of Eden. 

Thus, the so-called "War" is, in one of its many meanings, an allegorical record of the conflict between two classes of **Adepts** <note>Highly advanced spiritual masters</note>—those of the Right-Hand Path and those of the Left-Hand Path. In India, there were three classes of **Rishis** <note>Enlightened seers</note> who were the earliest known Adepts: 
1. The Royal Sages, or **Râjarshis**, who were kings and princes who adopted a life of spiritual discipline <note>original: "ascetic life"</note>. 
2. The Divine Sages, or **Devarshis**, who were the sons of Dharma (Righteousness) or Yoga. 
3. The Holy Sages, or **Brahmarshis**, who were descendants of those Rishis who founded the priestly lineages <note>original: "Gotras of Brâhmans"</note> or caste-races. 

Now, putting aside the mythical and astronomical interpretations for a moment, the secret teachings show that many people from **Atlantis** <note>original: "Atlanteans"</note> belonged to these groups, and there were actual conflicts and wars between them, **in fact and by law** <note>original: "de facto and de jure"</note>. **Nârada**, one of the greatest Rishis, was a Divine Sage (*Devarshi*); he is shown in an eternal feud with the creator-god Brahmâ, the patriarch Daksha, and other gods and sages. 

Therefore, we may safely maintain that whatever the astronomical meaning of this universally accepted legend may be, its human phase is based on real and historical events, which were distorted into religious dogma only to serve church purposes. As it is above, so it is below. The movements of the stars <note>original: "Sidereal phenomena"</note> and the behavior of the heavenly bodies were taken as a model, and the plan was carried out **below**, on Earth. Thus, Space, in its abstract sense, was called the "realm of divine knowledge." The Chaldeans (the ancient Mesopotamian Initiates) called it **Ab Soo**, meaning the "dwelling place" (or "father," meaning the "source") of knowledge, because it is in Space

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

Understanding the meaning of the Dragon is not granted to the "companions" (<term>Chelâs</term> <note>students or disciples in the esoteric tradition</note>), but only to the "little ones"—that is, the perfect <term>Initiates</term>.

The "companions" understand the work of the beginning; but only the "little ones" understand the parable regarding the work in the Beginning <note>original Latin: "Principium"</note> through the *Mystery of the Serpent of the Great Sea.**

Those Christians who happen to read this will also understand, by the light of the sentence above, who their "Christ" was. For Jesus states repeatedly that "whoever shall not receive the Kingdom of God as a *little child,* he shall not enter therein." While some of his sayings may have been meant to apply to actual children without metaphor, most of the references to the "little ones" in the Gospels relate to the Initiates, of whom Jesus was one. Paul (Saul) is even referred to in the *Talmud* as the "little one."

The "Mystery of the Serpent" was this: Our Earth, or rather terrestrial life, is often referred to in the Secret Teachings as the "Great Sea." The "Sea of Life" remains a favorite metaphor to this day. The *Book of Concealed Mystery* <note>original Hebrew: "Siphra Dtzenioutha," a foundational text of the Kabbalah</note> speaks of Primeval Chaos and the Evolution of the Universe after a Destruction (<term>Pralaya</term> <note>a period of cosmic rest or dissolution</note>), comparing it to an uncoiling serpent:

> Extending here and there, its tail in its mouth, its head twisting on its neck, it is enraged and angry. . . . It watches and conceals itself. Every thousand Days it is manifested.†

### A commentary on the *Purânas* <note>ancient Indian sacred texts</note> says:

> *Ananta-Shesha* is a form of Vishnu, the Holy Spirit of Preservation, and a symbol of the Universe, upon which he is supposed to sleep during the intervals of the *Days of Brahmâ.* The seven heads of Shesha support the Universe.

So the Spirit of God "sleeps," or "breathes" over the Chaos of Undifferentiated Matter before each new "Creation," says the *Book of Concealed Mystery.* Now, one "Day of Brahmâ" is composed, as already explained, of one thousand <term>Mahâ Yugas</term> <note>Great Ages; in Hindu cosmology, one Mahâ Yuga lasts 4,320,000 years</note>. "once in a thousand days." Nor is it more difficult to see where the initiated writer of the *Siphra* <note>The *Siphra Dtzenioutha*, or *Book of Concealed Mystery*, a foundational Kabbalistic text</note> is leading us, when he says:

This is a good reason why the Latin Church made him the patron saint of every promontory in Europe. In the *Siphra Dtzenioutha*, the Creative Force "makes sketches and spiral lines of his creation in the shape of a Serpent." It "holds its tail in its mouth" because it is the symbol of endless eternity and of cyclic periods. Its meanings, however, would require an entire volume to explain, and so we must end here.

Thus, the reader may now see for himself the various meanings of the "War in Heaven" and of the "Great Dragon." In this way, the most solemn and dreaded of Church dogmas—the <term>alpha and omega</term> <note>the beginning and the end</note> of the Christian faith, and the pillar of its "Fall of Man" and "Atonement"—dwindles down to a Pagan symbol found in the many allegories of these prehistoric struggles.

## SECTION 5.
### IS THE PLERÔMA SATAN'S LAIR?

The subject is not yet finished and must be examined from still other aspects.

Whether Milton's grand description of the three *days’* battle of the Angels of Light against those of Darkness justifies the suspicion that he must have heard of the corresponding Eastern tradition is impossible to say. Nevertheless, if he was not himself in connection with some <term>Mystic</term> <note>a person who seeks direct knowledge of spiritual truths through intuition or meditation</note>, then it must have been through someone who had obtained access to the secret works of the Vatican. Among these, there is a tradition concerning the “Beni Shamash”—the “Children of the Sun”—relating to the Eastern allegory. This tradition contains far more minute details in its *three-part version* than one can find in either the *Book of Enoch* or the much more recent *Revelation* of St. John concerning the “Old Dragon” and his various *Slayers*, as has just been shown.

It seems strange to find, even today, authors belonging to mystical societies who still maintain their preconceived doubts regarding the "alleged" antiquity of the *Book of Enoch*. For instance, while the author of *Sacred Mysteries among the Mayas and Quiches* is inclined to see Enoch as an <term>Initiate</term> <note>someone accepted into the study of secret spiritual knowledge</note> converted to Christianity (!),<note>original footnote: P. 16.</note> the English compiler of Éliphas Lévi’s works, *The Mysteries of Magic*, is of a similar opinion. > Aside from the scholarly work of Dr. Kenealy, no modern scholarship attributes any older antiquity to this work [the *Book of Enoch*] than the fourth century BCE.<note>original footnote: "Biographical and Critical Essay," p. xxxviii.</note>

Modern scholarship has been guilty of worse errors than this one. The "Old Dragon" and Satan, which have now become both individual and collective symbols for—and the theological terms for—the "Fallen Angel," are not described that way in either the *original* <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>A system of Jewish mysticism; the author refers here to the Chaldean *Book of Numbers*, a lost or secret text often cited in her works</note> or in the modern version. This description—one which so cunningly reconciles theological dogma and Kabbalistic allegory, and even manages to include a political compliment in its wording—is quite correct when read in the right spirit.

Yes, indeed; it is this grandest of ideals, this ever-living symbol—even the <term>apotheosis</term> <note>the elevation of someone to divine status; the perfect example</note>—of self-sacrifice for the intellectual independence of humanity. It is this ever-active Energy protesting against static inertia—the principle to which self-assertion is a crime, and thought and the light of knowledge are hateful. As Éliphas says with unparalleled justice and irony:

> It is this supposed hero of dark eternities, who, slanderously charged with ugliness, is decorated with horns and claws, which would much better fit his relentless tormentor.†

It is he who has been finally transformed into a Serpent—the Red Dragon. But Éliphas Lévi was still too subservient to his Roman Catholic authorities—and one may add, too deceptive—to admit that this "Devil" was actually mankind, and never had any existence on Earth outside of humanity itself.‡

The Church had to isolate itself and assert its authority. Therefore, it could do no better than to turn every Pagan deity into a devil. Every bright sun-god of antiquity—a glorious deity by day and its own opponent and adversary by night, called the "Dragon of Wisdom" because it was supposed to contain the seeds of both night and day—has now been turned into the antithetical "Shadow of God." It has become Satan based solely on the unsupported authority of human religious dogma. After this, all these producers of light and shadow, all the sun-gods and moon-gods, were cursed; thus, the one God chosen out of many and Satan have both been <term>anthropomorphized</term> <note>given human characteristics, emotions, or intentions</note>. 

But theology seems to have lost sight of the human capacity for discriminating and finally analyzing all that is artificially forced upon its reverence. History also proves that the God of the Israelites was such a *tribal God* and nothing more, even though the Christian Church—following the lead of the "chosen" people—is pleased to enforce the worship of that one particular deity and to <term>anathematize</term> <note>to formally curse or excommunicate</note> all the others. In antiquity, Jehovah was always only a God "among" other "gods."\* The *Lord* appears to Abraham, and while saying, "I am the Almighty God," he adds, "I will establish my covenant . . . . to be a God unto you" (Abraham); and unto *his descendants after him*†—but not unto Aryan Europeans.

However, there was then the grandiose and ideal figure of Jesus of Nazareth to be set against a dark background, so he might gain radiance by the contrast; *and the Church could hardly have invented a darker one*. Lacking the *Old Testament* symbology and ignorant of the real meaning of the name of Jehovah—the Rabbinical secret substitute for the Ineffable and Unpronounceable Name <note>This refers to the Tetragrammaton, YHWH, the four-letter name of God in Hebrew which was considered too holy to speak aloud</note>—the Church mistook the cunningly fabricated shadow for the reality. # JEHOVAH, A PERSONATING SPIRIT.

The author of *New Aspects of Life* describes the Jewish God very correctly from the kabbalistic <note>original: "kabalistic"; referring to the Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism</note> standpoint as:

> The Spirit of the Earth, which had revealed itself to the Jews as Jehovah.* . . . It was that Spirit again who, after the death of Jesus, assumed his form and personated him as the risen Christ.

—This is the doctrine of Cerinthus <note>an early Gnostic who taught that the "Christ" spirit descended upon the man Jesus at his baptism and left before his crucifixion</note> and several Gnostic <note>an early Christian-era movement that emphasized secret, experiential knowledge over blind faith</note> sects with slight variation, as one can see. But the author’s explanations and deductions are remarkable:

> No one knew . . . better than Moses, . . . [and] so well as he, how great was the power of those [Gods of Egypt] with whose priests he had contended, . . . the gods of which Jehovah is claimed to be the God [by the Jews only].

The author asks:

> What were these gods, these "Achar" <note>original: "Achar"; Hebrew for "Other," referring to "other gods" (Elohim Acharim)</note> of which Jehovah, the "Achad" <note>original: "Achad"; Hebrew for "One," specifically the "One God"</note>, is claimed to be the God . . . by overcoming them?

To which our Occultism answers: They are those whom the Church now calls the Fallen Angels and collectively Satan, the Dragon—overcome, if we have to accept *her* verdict, by Michael and his Host. That Michael is simply Jehovah himself, who is one of the subordinate Spirits at best. Therefore, the author is again right in saying:

> The Greeks believed in the existence of . . . *daimons* <note>original: "daimons"; ancient Greek spirits that could be good or evil, not necessarily "demons" in the modern sense</note>. But . . . they were anticipated by the Hebrews, who held that *there was a class of personating spirits which they designated demons*, or "personators." . . . Admitting with Jehovah, who expressly asserts it, the existence of other gods, which . . . were personators of the One God—were these other gods simply a higher class of personating spirits, . . . which had acquired and exercised greater powers? And is not personation <term>the key to the mystery of the spirit state?</term> But once granting this position, *how are we to know that Jehovah was not a personating spirit*, a spirit which claimed for itself that it was, and thus became, the personator of the one unknown and unknowable God? In fact, how do we know that the spirit calling itself Jehovah, in claiming his attributes for itself, did not thus cause its own name to be attributed to the One who is in reality as nameless as he is unknowable?†

Then the author shows that “the spirit Jehovah is a personator” by its own admission. It acknowledged to Moses “that it had appeared to the patriarchs as the God Shaddai” <note>original: "Shaddai"; usually translated as "Almighty"</note> and the “God Helion” <note>original: "Helion" (Elyon); usually translated as "Most High"</note>.

In the same breath, it assumed the name of Jehovah; and it is based on the assertion of this personator that the names El, Eloah, Elohim, and Shaddai have been read and interpreted in connection with Jehovah as the “Lord God Almighty.” [Then when] the name Jehovah became <term>ineffable</term> <note>too sacred to be spoken aloud</note>, the designation Adonai, meaning “Lord,” was substituted for it, and . . . it was owing to this substitution—
