# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

By moving past the previous interpretation, the symbol is made to reveal a portion of its mysteries with the help of the astronomical key, offering a more metaphysical rendering. The <term>Ankh-tie</term> <note>The Egyptian "handled cross" or symbol of life</note> ☥ does not belong to Egypt alone. It exists under the name of <term>Pâsha</term> <note>Sanskrit for "noose" or "cord"</note>, a cord which the four-armed <term>Shiva</term> holds in his back right hand.* The <term>Mahâdeva</term> <note>the "Great God," an epithet of Shiva</note> is represented in the posture of an ascetic, as <term>Mahâyogî</term> <note>the "Great Yogi"</note>, with his <term>third eye</term> (◴), which is "the Ru ☉ <note>The Egyptian hieroglyph representing an opening or mouth</note>, set upright on the <term>Tau-cross</term>" ☨ in another form. The <term>Pâsha</term> is held in the hand in such a way that the index finger and the part of the hand near the thumb create a cross, or a loop and a crossing. Our Orientalists <note>19th-century Western scholars of Eastern cultures</note> would have us believe it represents a cord for binding stubborn <note>original: "refractory"</note> offenders, simply because <term>Kâli</term>, Shiva’s consort, has the same object as an attribute!

<image-desc>A detailed illustration of a human hand, possibly Shiva's, holding a looped rope, symbolizing the Pâsha.</image-desc>

The <term>Pâsha</term> has a double significance here, as does Shiva’s <term>Trisûla</term> <note>trident</note> and every other divine attribute. This dual significance lies within <term>Shiva</term> himself, for <term>Rudra</term> <note>an earlier, fiercer Vedic form of Shiva</note> certainly carries the same meaning as the Egyptian <term>Ansated Cross</term> <note>the Ankh</note> in its cosmic and mystic sense. In the hand of <term>Shiva</term>, the <term>Pâsha</term> becomes <term>lingyonic</term> <note>symbolizing the union of the male (lingam) and female (yoni) generative principles</note>. <term>Shiva</term>, as mentioned before, is a name unknown to the *Vedas* <note>the oldest scriptures of Hinduism</note>. It is in the *White Yajur Veda* that <term>Rudra</term> appears for the first time as the <term>Great God</term>, <term>Mahâdeva</term>, whose symbol is the <term>Lingam</term>. In the *Rig Veda*, he is called <term>Rudra</term>, the "howler," a deity who is both beneficent and harmful at the same time—the <term>Healer</term> and the <term>Destroyer</term>.

In the *Vishnu Purâna*, he is the <term>God</term> who springs from the forehead of <term>Brahmâ</term> and separates into male and female forms. He is the parent of the <term>Rudras</term> or <term>Maruts</term> <note>storm deities</note>, half of whom are brilliant and gentle, while the others are black and ferocious. In the *Vedas*, he represents the <term>Divine Ego</term> aspiring to return to its pure, divine state; yet, he is simultaneously that <term>Divine Ego</term> imprisoned in an earthly form, whose fierce passions make him the "roarer" and the "terrible." This is clearly shown in the *Brihadâranyaka Upanishad*, where the <term>Rudras</term> (the offspring of <term>Rudra</term>, the <term>God of Fire</term>) are called the "ten vital breaths (<term>prâna</term>, life), with the heart-mind (<term>manas</term>) as the eleventh,"† whereas as <term>Shiva</term>, he is the *destroyer* of that life. <term>Brahmâ</term> calls him <term>Rudra</term> and gives him seven other names, signifying seven forms of manifestation and the seven powers of nature that destroy only to recreate or regenerate.

# THE HEAVENLY "PORPOISE."

Shiva is represented as an ascetic, the <term>Mahâyogin</term> <note>the "Great Yogi," a title for Shiva as the patron of meditation and yoga</note>, and this has no phallic meaning. Indeed, it requires an imagination strongly inclined in that direction to find such a meaning even in an astronomical symbol. As an emblem of a "door, gate, mouth, or the place of outlet," it signifies the "narrow gate" that leads to the Kingdom of Heaven far more than a "birthplace" in a physical <note>original: "physiological"</note> sense.

It is indeed a cross within a circle and a <term>Crux Ansata</term> <note>Latin: "handled cross," referring to the Egyptian Ankh symbol ☥</note>. However, it is a cross upon which all human passions must be sacrificed <note>original: "crucified"</note> before the <term>Yogî</term> passes through the "narrow gate"—that small circle which expands into an infinite one as soon as the Inner Man has crossed the threshold.

As for the mysterious seven <term>Rishis</term> <note>sages or seers in Hindu tradition</note> in the constellation of the Great Bear: while Egypt made them sacred to "the oldest mother, <term>Typhon</term> <note>an Egyptian deity associated with chaos and storms</note>," India has connected these symbols for ages with Time or <term>Yuga</term>-revolutions. These <term>Saptarshis</term> <note>the "Seven Rishis"</note> are intimately connected with our present age—the dark <term>Kali Yuga</term>.* The great Circle of Time, upon which Indian tradition has represented the Porpoise, or <term>Shishu-mâra</term> <note>Sanskrit for "child-killer," a name for the constellation of the dolphin or porpoise, often identified with the celestial sphere</note>, has the cross placed on it by nature through the division and positioning of stars, planets, and constellations. In the *Bhâgavata Purâna*,† it is said:

> At the tip of the tail of that animal, whose head is directed toward the south and whose body is in the shape of a ring [circle], <term>Dhruva</term> [the Pole Star] is placed; along its tail are <term>Prajâpati</term>, <term>Agni</term>, <term>Indra</term>, <term>Dharma</term>, etc.; *across its loins are the seven Rishis.*‡

This is then the first and earliest cross and circle formed by the Deity, symbolized by <term>Vishnu</term>—the Eternal Circle of Boundless Time, <term>Kâla</term>. Upon this plane lie crossways all the gods, creatures, and creations born in Space and Time—who, as the Philosophy teaches, all die at the <term>Mahâpralaya</term> <note>the "Great Dissolution" or end of a cosmic cycle</note>.

Meanwhile, it is the seven Rishis who mark the time and the duration of events in our sevenfold life-cycle. They are as mysterious as their supposed wives, the <term>Pleiades</term>, of whom only one—she who hides—has proven virtuous. The Pleiades, or <term>Krittikâs</term>, are the nurses of <term>Kârttikeya</term>, the God of War (the <term>Mars</term> of the Western pagans). He is called the Commander of the Celestial Armies, or rather of the <term>Siddhas</term> <note>perfected or holy beings</note>—<term>Siddha-sena</term> (translated as Yogis in Heaven and holy Sages on Earth). This would make Kârttikeya identical with <term>Michael</term>, the "Leader of—"

One point is worth mentioning in this question of the cross and circle, as it relates strongly to the elements of Fire and Water, which play such an important part in circle and cross symbolism.

Like Mars—who is alleged by the Roman poet Ovid to have been born of his mother Juno alone, without a father—or like the <term>Avatâras</term> <note>divine incarnations</note> (such as Krishna) in both the West and the East, Kârttikeya is born in a still more miraculous manner. # THE RISHIS AND THE PLEIADES.

This method involved assuming an imaginary line, or a "great circle," passing through the poles of the ecliptic and the beginning of the fixed lunar mansion <term>Maghâ</term> <note>Sanskrit: one of the 27 lunar mansions (nakshatras) in Hindu astronomy, associated with the star Regulus</note>. This circle was supposed to intersect some of the stars in the Great Bear. Since the seven stars in the Great Bear are called the **Rishis**, the line assumed in this way was called the "Line of the **Rishis**." Because this line was permanently fixed to the beginning of the lunar asterism Maghâ, the precession of the equinoxes could be recorded by stating the degree of any movable lunar mansion intersected by that line or circle, using it as an index.*

There has been, and there still exists, a seemingly endless controversy regarding the chronology of the Hindus. However, here is a point that could help determine—at least approximately—the age when the symbolism of the seven **Rishis** and their connection with the Pleiades began. When the gods delivered the deity **Kârttikeya** to the **Krittikâ** <note>the Sanskrit name for the Pleiades</note> to be nursed, there were only six nurses; this is why Kârttikeya is represented with six heads. But when the poetic imagination of the early **Aryan** symbologists turned them into the wives of the seven **Rishis**, they became **seven**. 

Their names are given as Amba, Dulâ, Nitatui, Abrayanti, Maghâyanti, Varshayanti, and Chupunika, though other sets of names exist which differ. In any case, the seven **Rishis** were said to marry the seven **Krittikâ** before the "disappearance" of the seventh Pleiad. Otherwise, how could the Hindu astronomers speak of a star which **no one** can see without the help of the strongest telescopes? This mystery is perhaps why, in every such case, the majority of the events described in Hindu allegories are dismissed by critics as "a very recent invention, certainly created *within* the Christian era."

The oldest Sanskrit manuscripts on astronomy begin their series of **Nakshatras**—the twenty-seven lunar asterisms—with the sign of **Krittikâ**. This placement can hardly make these texts earlier than 2,780 B.C. This date is according to the "Vedic Calendar," which is accepted even by <term>Orientalists</term> <note>19th-century Western scholars of Eastern languages and cultures</note>. However, these scholars get out of the difficulty by claiming that this calendar does not *prove* that the Hindus knew anything about astronomy at that date. They assure their readers that, despite the calendars, the Indian scholars (Pandits) may have acquired their knowledge of the lunar mansions starting with Krittikâ from the Phoenicians or other cultures. 

Regardless of its origin, the Pleiades are the central group in the system of sidereal <note>star-based</note> symbolism. They are situated in the "neck" of the constellation Taurus. In astronomy, they are regarded by Mädler and others as the **central group** of the system of the Milky Way. In the **Kabalah** and **Eastern Esotericism**, they are seen as the **sidereal seven** <note>original: "sidereal septenate"</note> born from the first manifested side of the upper triangle—the concealed equilateral triangle: <note>original: image of a small equilateral triangle</note>. This manifested side is Taurus, the symbol of One

(the number 1), or of the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, **Aleph** (א) meaning "bull" or "ox." Its synthesis is **Ten** (10), or **Yod** (י), which is considered the perfect letter and number. The **Pleiades** (and especially the star **Alcyone**) are regarded, even in modern astronomy, as the central point around which *our universe of fixed stars revolves*. <note>This refers to the 19th-century "Central Sun" hypothesis, which suggested the Pleiades were the gravitational center of the Milky Way.</note> In Occult Philosophy, they are the focus from which, and into which, the Divine Breath and Motion work incessantly during the **Manvantara** <term>Manvantara</term> <note>Sanskrit: a period of cosmic activity or manifestation, as opposed to a period of rest (Pralaya)</note>. Therefore, in the celestial symbols of the Occult Philosophy, the circle with the starry cross on its face plays the most prominent role.

The Secret Doctrine teaches us that everything in the Universe, as well as the Universe itself, is formed ("created") during its periodical manifestations. This occurs through accelerated **Motion** set into activity by the **Breath** of the Power that is "ever-to-be-unknown"—at least to present-day mankind—within the world of appearances. The Spirit of Life and Immortality was everywhere symbolized by a circle. Because of this, the serpent biting its tail represents the Circle of Wisdom in Infinity. The same meaning is found in the astronomical cross (the cross within a circle) and the globe with two wings added to it. This later became the sacred **Scarabaeus** <note>original: "Scarabæus"</note> of the Egyptians, its very name suggesting the secret idea attached to it. 

In Egyptian papyri, the Scarabaeus is called *Khopirron* and *Khopri* from the verb *khopron*, meaning "to become." It was thus made a symbol and an emblem of human life and of the successive "becomings" of man. These "becomings" refer to the various journeys and transmigrations of the soul, or the **reincarnations** of the liberated soul. This mystical symbol shows plainly that the Egyptians believed in reincarnation and the successive lives and existences of the Immortal Entity. However, as this was an **Esoteric Doctrine** <note>Hidden or inner teaching</note> revealed only during the Mysteries by the high priests and the initiate-kings to the candidates, it was kept secret. 

The **Incorporeal Intelligences** (the Planetary Spirits or Creative Powers) were always represented in the form of circles. In the primitive philosophy of the high priests, these *invisible* circles were the original causes and builders of all the heavenly orbs. The stars and planets were merely their *visible* bodies or coverings, of which the circles were the souls. This was certainly a universal teaching in antiquity.* As **Proclus** <note>A Greek Neoplatonist philosopher (412–485 AD) who wrote extensively on mathematics and philosophy</note> says:

> Before the mathematical numbers, there are the *self-moving numbers*; before the visible figures, there are the life-giving figures. Before producing the material worlds which move in a circle, the **Creative Power produced the invisible circles**.†

<header>THE SUPREME GOOD OF PLATO.</header>

"Monarch" and "Law-giver of the Universe" carry an abstract meaning well understood by every <term>Occultist</term> <note>A student of hidden or esoteric knowledge concerning the laws of nature and the universe.</note>. Like any Christian, the occultist believes in the One Law that governs the Universe and recognizes it as unchangeable. As Plato says:

Beyond all finite existences and secondary causes, all laws, ideas, and principles, there is an Intelligence or Mind <note>original: *nous* (νοῦς)</note>, the first principle of all principles, the Supreme Idea on which all other ideas are grounded... the ultimate substance from which all things derive their being and essence, the First and efficient Cause of all the order, harmony, beauty, excellence, and goodness which pervade the Universe.

This Mind is called, with the highest distinction, the Supreme Good,* "The God" <note>original: *ho theos* (ὁ θεός)</note>, and the "God over all." These words apply, as Plato himself shows, neither to the "Creator" nor to the "Father" of our modern monotheists, but to the <term>Ideal and Abstract Cause</term>. For, as he says: "This *theos* <note>original: *theos* (θεός), meaning God</note>, the God over all, is *not the truth or the intelligence, but the Father of it*," and its Primal Cause. 

Could Plato—the greatest pupil of the ancient Sages and a Sage himself, for whom the only goal in life was Real Knowledge—ever have believed in a Deity that curses and damns men forever on the slightest provocation?† Certainly not he, for he considered only those who possessed the knowledge of *what really exists* (as opposed to mere appearance) to be genuine philosophers and seekers of truth. These are the ones who seek that which *always exists* in opposition to the transitory; and that which exists permanently in opposition to that which grows, fades, develops, and is destroyed in turn.‡ 

Speusippus and Xenocrates followed in his footsteps. The One, the original source, had no "existence" in the sense applied to it by mortal men. The <term>honored one</term> <note>original: *timion* (τίμιον)</note> dwells in the center as much as in the circumference, but it is only the reflection of the Deity—the <term>World Soul</term> <note>The spiritual essence that pervades all nature</note>§—the surface plane of the circle. # THE RIDDLE OF THE CROSS.

From it [the circle] comes their Swastika <note>original: "Svastika"</note>, which is now the *Wan* <note>The Chinese name for the swastika symbol.</note> of the Mongolian Buddhist. ->THE SLEEP OF SILOAM.<-

...comes from Egypt, and primarily from India. This puzzle can only be solved by searching for its key in the Mysteries of Initiation <term>ancient secret rituals used to admit someone into a religious or philosophical group</term>. The initiated Adept <term>a master of secret knowledge</term>, who had successfully passed through all the trials, was attached—*not nailed*, but simply tied—to a couch in the shape of a Tau (T) in Egypt, or a Swastika <note>original: "Svastika"</note> without the four additional extensions (a + rather than 卐) in India. He was then plunged into a deep sleep—the "Sleep of Siloam," as it is still called today among the initiates in Asia Minor, Syria, and even Upper Egypt. 

He was allowed to remain in this state for three days and three nights. During this time, his Spiritual Ego was said to commune <note>original: "confabulate"</note> with the "Gods," descend into the underworld—Hades, Amenti <term>the ancient Egyptian underworld</term>, or Pâtâla <term>the underworld in Hindu cosmology</term>, depending on the country—and perform works of charity for invisible beings, whether the souls of humans or elemental spirits. Meanwhile, his body remained in a temple crypt or underground cave. In Egypt, the body was placed in the sarcophagus within the King’s Chamber of the Pyramid of Cheops. During the night leading into the third day, it was carried to the entrance of a gallery. At a specific hour, the rays of the rising sun would strike directly on the face of the entranced candidate, who would then wake to be initiated by Osiris and Thoth, the God of Wisdom.

If you doubt this statement, please consult the original Hebrew texts before rejecting it. Look at certain very suggestive Egyptian *bas-reliefs* <term>sculptures where figures project slightly from a flat background</term>. One in particular, from the temple of Philae, represents a *scene of initiation*. Two high priests representing gods—one with the head of a hawk (representing the Sun) and the other with the head of an ibis (representing Mercury or Thoth, the God of Wisdom and Secret Learning, and the companion of Osiris-Sun)—are standing over the body of a candidate who has just been initiated. # THE REAL OUR FATHER <note>original: "Paternoster"</note>.

Later, due to the gradual loss of spiritual understanding, the cross came to represent nothing more than a *phallic symbol* <note>An image representing the generative or creative powers of nature</note> in theories regarding the origin of the universe and human development.

According to Esotericists <note>Students of hidden or secret wisdom</note> from the most ancient times, the Universal Soul—or the *Soul of the World* <note>original Latin: "Anima Mundi"</note>, which is the material reflection of the immaterial Ideal—was the source of life for all beings and the life-principle of the three kingdoms of nature. This principle was *sevenfold* <note>original: "septenary"</note> according to the Hermetic Philosophers <note>Followers of the mystical traditions attributed to Hermes Trismegistus</note>, just as it was for all ancient peoples. It is represented as a seven-branched cross, whose arms symbolize *light, heat, electricity, earth-based magnetism, astral radiation, motion, and intelligence* (or what some call self-awareness).

As we have noted elsewhere, long before the cross or its image were adopted as symbols of Christianity, the sign of the cross was used as a mark of recognition among Adepts <note>Highly advanced spiritual masters</note> and Neophytes <note>Beginners or initiates in a secret society</note>. These neophytes were called "Chrests"—from the Greek *Chrestos* <note>Meaning "excellent" or "holy," often associated here with the initiate undergoing trials</note>, the man of trials and sorrow. Éliphas Lévi <note>A famous 19th-century French occultist</note> says:

> The sign of the cross adopted by Christians does not belong to them alone. It is also Kabbalistic and represents the opposition and four-part equilibrium of the elements. We see by the secret verse of the *Our Father* <note>original: "Paternoster"</note> . . . that there were originally two ways of performing it, or at least *two* very different formulas to express its meaning: one reserved for the priests and initiates, and the other given to the beginners and the uninitiated <note>original: "profane"</note>. For example, the initiate, bringing his hand to his forehead, said, "*To you*"; then added, "*belong*"; and continued, moving his hand to the chest, "*the kingdom*"; then to the left shoulder, "*justice*"; and to the right shoulder, "*and mercy*." Then he joined his hands, adding, "*throughout the cycles of creation—To You are the Kingdom, the Power, and the Mercy through the Ages*" <note>original Latin/Hebrew: "Tibi sunt Malchut et Geburah et Chesed per Æonas"</note>. This is an absolute and magnificent Kabbalistic sign of the cross, which the official Church lost completely due to the corruptions of Gnosticism <note>A diverse group of early religious movements that emphasized personal spiritual knowledge</note>.\*

The "militant and official Church" did even more: having taken what never belonged to her, she took only what the uninitiated had—the Kabbalistic meaning of the *male* and *female* Sephiroth <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note>. She never lost the *inner* and higher meaning because she never possessed it—despite Éliphas Lévi’s attempts to flatter the Roman Church. The sign of the cross adopted by the Latin <note>Roman Catholic</note> Church was *phallic* from the start, while the cross of the Greek Church was the cross of the spiritual seekers, the *Chrestoi*.

## SECTION IX.
### The Upanishads in Gnostic Literature.
---

We are reminded in C.W. King's *The Gnostics and Their Remains* that the Greek language had only one word for both *vowel* and *voice*. This has led the uninitiated <note>those without specialized or secret knowledge</note> to many incorrect interpretations. However, based on the simple knowledge of this well-known fact, a comparison may be attempted, and a flood of light can be thrown upon several mystical meanings. Thus, the words "Sound" and "Speech," which are so often used in the *Upanishads* <note>ancient Sanskrit texts containing the central philosophical concepts of Hinduism</note> and the *Puranas* <note>vast anthologies of Indian folklore, history, and philosophy</note>, may be compared with the Gnostic "Vowels" and the "Voices" of the Thunders and Angels in the biblical Book of *Revelation*. The same connection will be found in the *Faith-Wisdom* <note>original: "Pistis Sophia," a significant Gnostic scripture</note> and other ancient fragments and manuscripts. This was remarked upon even by the matter-of-fact author of the work mentioned above.

Through Hippolytus, an early Church Father, we learn what Marcus—a follower of Pythagoras <note>an ancient Greek philosopher</note> rather than a Christian Gnostic, and certainly a student of the Kabbalah <note>original: "Kabalist"</note>—had received in a mystical revelation. It is said that Marcus had it revealed to him that:

> The *seven heavens** . . . each sounded one vowel, which, all combined together, formed a single song of praise <note>original: "doxology"</note>, "the *sound* of which, being carried down [from these seven heavens] to earth, becomes the creator and parent of all things that exist on earth."†

Translated from hidden <note>original: "Occult"</note> terminology into even plainer language, this would read: The Sevenfold Divine Words <note>original: "Logoi"</note> having divided into seven "Words," or Creative Powers (Vowels), these (the Second "Word" or "Sound") created everything on Earth.

# THE SEVEN THUNDERS.

Seven thunders spoke . . . . [and] I was about to write . . . . [but] I heard a voice from heaven saying to me, "Seal up those things which the seven thunders spoke, and do not write them."*

The same instruction is given to Marcus <note>a Gnostic teacher and follower of Valentinus</note>, and to all other partial and full Initiates <note>those admitted into secret or sacred knowledge</note>. The very similarity of the expressions used, and of the underlying ideas, always reveals a portion of the Mysteries. We must always seek more than one meaning in every mystery revealed through allegory, especially in those where the number seven and its square (seven times seven, or forty-nine) appear. Now, when in the *Faith-Wisdom* <note>original: "Pistis Sophia," a key Gnostic text</note>, the Rabbi Jesus is requested by his disciples to reveal to them the "Mysteries of the Light of his Father"—meaning the Higher Self enlightened by Initiation and Divine Knowledge—Jesus answers:

> Do you seek after these mysteries? No mystery is more excellent than they; they shall bring your souls into the Light of Lights, into the place of Truth and Goodness, into the place where there is neither male nor female, nor any form, but only everlasting Light that cannot be described. Nothing, therefore, is more excellent than the mysteries you seek, except only the mystery of the seven Vowels and their forty-nine Powers, and their specific numbers. And no name is more excellent than all these (Vowels).†

As the Commentary says when speaking of the "Fires":
> *The Seven Fathers and the Forty-nine Sons blaze in Darkness, but they are the Life and Light and the continuation of that Light through the Great Age.*

It now becomes evident that in every internal <note>original: "Esoteric"</note> interpretation of outward <note>original: "exoteric"</note> beliefs expressed in allegorical forms, there is the same underlying idea—the basic number **seven**, which is the sum of **three** and **four**, preceded by the divine three (<image-desc>equilateral triangle symbol</image-desc>) making the perfect number **ten**.

Also, these numbers apply equally to divisions of time, to the structure of the universe (both metaphysical and physical), as well as to humanity and everything else in visible Nature. Thus, these seven Vowels with their forty-nine Powers are identical to the "three and the seven Fires" of the Hindus and their "forty-nine Fires"; they are also identical to the numerical mysteries of the Persian Simorgh <note>a benevolent, mythical bird in Persian mythology</note> and those of the Jewish Kabbalists. They claimed the seven Renewals of the Globe lasted only 7,000 years, instead of the more likely 7,000,000,000 years, and assigned a total duration of only 49,000 years to the entire Universe.‡

Now, the Secret Doctrine provides a key which reveals to us—based on the indisputable grounds of comparative analogy—that <term>Garuda</term> <note>a divine eagle-like being in Hindu mythology</note>, the symbolic and magnificent half-man and half-bird, is the origin of all such allegories. > Whatever its primary meaning [of the gem with the solar lion and vowels], it was probably imported in its current form from India (that true fountainhead of Gnostic art).§

### PISTIS SOPHIA.
<note>original: Πίστις Σοφία; the title translates to "Faith-Wisdom"</note>

Even in the *Book of Revelation*.* When the seven “Thunders,” or “Sounds,” or “Vowels”—one meaning out of the seven for each vowel relates directly to our own Earth and its seven <term>Root-Races</term> <note>In Theosophy, these are the seven major stages of human evolution during a planetary cycle</note> in each Round—“had uttered their voices,” the Seer was forbidden to write them down and was told to “seal up those things.” What did the Angel, “standing upon the sea and upon the earth,” do then?

He lifted up his hand to heaven and swore by him who lives forever and ever . . . that there should be *time no longer*: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound, the mystery of God [of the Cycle] should be finished.†

In Theosophical terms, this means that when the Seventh Round is completed, Time will cease. “There shall be time no longer”—quite naturally, since <term>Pralaya</term> <note>original: Sanskrit for "dissolution"; a period of rest or non-existence between cycles of manifestation</note> shall set in. There will remain no one on Earth to keep a division of time during that periodic dissolution and arrest of conscious life.

Dr. Kenealy and others believed that the calculations of the cyclic seven and forty-nine were brought by the <term>Rabbis</term> <note>original: "Rabbins"</note> from Chaldea. This is more than likely. However, the Babylonians—who possessed all those cycles and taught them only at their great initiation mysteries of astrological Magic—obtained their wisdom and learning from India. It is not difficult, therefore, to recognize our own <term>Esoteric Doctrine</term> <note>The hidden or "inner" spiritual teachings underlying all religions</note> within them. In their secret calculations, the Japanese have the same figures in their cycles. As for the Brahmins, their *Puranas* and *Upanishads* provide good proof of this. The latter have passed entirely into Gnostic literature; a Brahmin needs only to read *Pistis Sophia*‡ to recognize his forefathers’ property, right down to the phrasing and metaphors used. Let us compare them. In *Pistis Sophia*, the disciples say to Jesus:

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

...another baptism of *smoke*, and another baptism of the Spirit of Holy Light <note>original: i.e. the Spirit of Fire</note>.*

As <term>John the Baptist</term> says of <term>Jesus</term>:

> I indeed baptize you with water; . . . but he shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note> and with fire.

The real significance of this statement is very profound. It means that <term>John</term>, a non-initiated ascetic, can impart to his disciples no greater wisdom than the <term>Mysteries</term> connected with the plane of <term>Matter</term>, of which <term>Water</term> is the symbol. His <term>Gnosis</term> <note>original: Greek for "knowledge," referring to spiritual insight</note> was that of <term>exoteric</term> <note>public or outer teachings</note> and ritualistic dogma, of "dead-letter" orthodoxy;† while the wisdom which <term>Jesus</term>, an <term>Initiate</term> of the Higher Mysteries, would reveal to them was of a higher character, for it was the "Fire" Wisdom of the true <term>Gnosis</term> or *real* Spiritual Enlightenment. One was "Fire," the other the "Smoke." For <term>Moses</term>, there was the Fire on Mount Sinai and Spiritual Wisdom; for the multitudes of the "people" below—the uninitiated—Mount Sinai was seen only through Smoke: the outer husks of orthodox or sectarian ritualism.

Now, keeping the above in view, read the dialogue between the sages <term>Nârada</term> and <term>Devamata</term> in the <term>Anugîtâ</term>,‡ an episode from the <term>Mahâbhârata</term> <note>a major ancient Indian epic</note>. The antiquity and importance of this text can be found in the "Sacred Books of the East," edited by Professor <term>Max Müller</term>.§ <term>Nârada</term> is discoursing upon the "breaths" or the "life-winds," as they are called in the clumsy translations of words such as <term>Prâna</term> and <term>Apâna</term> <note>Sanskrit terms for vital life energies or breaths</note>, whose full <term>Esoteric</term> <note>inner or hidden</note> meaning and application to individual functions can hardly be expressed in English. He says of this science that:

> It is the teaching of the <term>Veda</term> that the *fire* truly is all the deities, and knowledge of it arises among <term>Brahmans</term>, being accompanied by intelligence.||

By "fire," says the Commentator, he means the <term>Self</term>. By "intelligence," the Occultist says, <term>Nârada</term> meant neither "discussion" nor "argumentation" (as <term>Arjuna Mishra</term> believes), but true "intelligence"—the adaptation of the *Fire of Wisdom* to outer ritualism for the uninitiated. This was the chief concern of the <term>Brahmans</term>, who were the first to set the example to other nations who thus anthropomorphized <note>gave human characteristics to divine or abstract concepts</note>...

->TRUTH BETWEEN TWO CONTRASTS.<-

...and made the grandest metaphysical truths physical and material. <term>Nârada</term> <note>A wise sage in Hindu mythology often depicted as a messenger between gods and humans</note> shows this plainly and is made to say:

> The smoke of that (fire) which is of excellent glory (appears) in the shape of . . . . darkness [truly!]; its ashes, . . . [are] passion; and . . . . goodness is that in connection with it, in which the offering is thrown.\*

This means that the disciple possesses a faculty that understands the subtle truth (the flame) rising toward heaven, while the physical sacrifice serves as evidence of piety only to the uninitiated. For what else could <term>Nârada</term> mean by the following?

> Those who understand the sacrifice understand the <term>Samâna</term> and the <term>Vyâna</term> <note>two of the five "life-winds" or vital energies in Hindu physiology</note> as the *principal* (offering). The <term>Prâna</term> and <term>Apâna</term> <note>the breaths of inspiration and expiration</note> are portions of the offering, . . . and between them is the fire. That is the excellent seat of the <term>Udâna</term> <note>the vital energy that rules the throat and upper body</note> as understood by <term>Brahmins</term>. Regarding that which is distinct from these pairs, listen to me speak. Day and night are a pair; between them is the fire. . . . That which *exists* and that which *does not exist* are a pair; between them is the fire. . . .†

And after every such contrast, <term>Nârada</term> adds:

> That is the excellent seat of the <term>Udâna</term> as understood by <term>Brahmins</term>.

Now many people do not know the full meaning of the statement that <term>Samâna</term>, <term>Vyâna</term>, <term>Prâna</term>, and <term>Apâna</term>—which are explained as "life-winds," but which we define as spiritual principles and their respective faculties and senses—are offered up to <term>Udâna</term>. <term>Udâna</term> is the so-called <note>original: "soi-disant"</note> principal "life-wind," which is said to function at all the joints. Therefore, a reader who does not realize that the word "Fire" in these allegories refers to both the "Self" and higher Divine Knowledge will understand nothing here. They will entirely miss the point of our argument, just as the translator and even the editor—the great Oxford Sanskrit scholar <term>F. Max Müller</term>—have missed the true meaning of <term>Nârada’s</term> words. On a literal, public level <note>original: "exoterically"</note>, this list of "life-winds" has roughly the meaning suggested in the footnotes, namely:

> The meaning *appears* to be this: The course of worldly life is due to the operations of the life-winds, which are attached to the self and lead to its manifestation as individual souls [?]. Of these, the <term>Samâna</term> and <term>Vyâna</term> are controlled and held in check by the <term>Prâna</term> and <term>Apâna</term>. . . . The latter two are held in check and controlled by the <term>Udâna</term>, which thus controls all. And the control of this, which is the control of all five, . . . leads to the supreme self.‡

The above is given as an explanation of the text, which records the words of the <term>Brahmin</term>. He narrates how he reached the ultimate Wisdom of <term>Yoga</term> <note>original: "Yogism"</note>, and in this way reached all-encompassing knowledge. Saying

<header>THE ANTIQUITY OF THE KAPILAS.</header>

## THE ANTIQUITY OF THE KAPILAS.

Next, we consider the descendants of Garuda <note>a legendary bird-like creature and the mount of the god Vishnu</note>. Then there is Diti, the mother of the Maruts <note>storm deities</note>, whose descendants and offspring belonged to the lineage of Hiranyaksha, "whose number was 77 <term>crores</term> <note>a unit in the Indian numbering system equal to ten million; thus, 770 million</note> of men," according to the *Padma Purana* <note>one of the eighteen major Puranas, or ancient Hindu texts</note>. All such narratives are dismissed by modern scholars as "meaningless fictions" and absurdities. But truth is the daughter of time, indeed; and time will eventually prove it.

Meanwhile, what could be easier than an attempt, at least, to verify <term>Puranic</term> <note>relating to the Puranas, ancient Indian records of history, mythology, and philosophy</note> chronology? There are many individuals named Kapila; but the Kapila who killed King Sagara's offspring—60,000 men strong—was undeniably the Kapila who founded the <term>Sankhya philosophy</term> <note>one of the six major schools of Hindu philosophy, focusing on the dualism between consciousness and matter</note>, as stated in the *Puranas*. This is true even though one of those texts flatly denies the accusation without explaining its <term>Esoteric</term> <note>intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge</note> meaning. It is the *Bhagavata Purana* which states:

> The report is not true that the king's sons were burned by the wrath of the sage. For how can the quality of darkness <note>original: *tamas*, the quality of ignorance or inertia</note>, which is the product of anger, exist in a Sage whose very nature was goodness and who purified the world—as if the earth's dust were elevated to the heavens? How should mental distress distract that sage, who is identified with the Supreme Spirit? He has steered the sturdy vessel of the Sankhya philosophy here on earth, by which anyone who desires liberation crosses the dreaded ocean of existence—that path which leads to death. <note>From Burnouf's Translation; see Wilson's *Vishnu Purana*, volume 3, page 300.</note>

The *Purana* is obligated to speak in this manner. It has a dogma to promote and a policy to maintain—that of extreme secrecy regarding mystical, divine truths which have been revealed only during <term>Initiation</term> <note>sacred ceremonies where secret knowledge is passed to a student</note> for countless ages. Therefore, we should not look to the *Puranas* for a direct explanation of the mystery concerning various transcendental states of being. The story is clearly an allegory: the 60,000 "sons," who are described as brutal, vicious, and wicked, are the personification of human passions. These passions are reduced to ashes by a "mere glance of the Sage"—representing the Higher Self, which is the highest state of purity achievable on Earth. However, the story also contains other meanings, including cyclic and chronological data used to mark the periods when certain Sages lived, which are also found in other *Puranas*.

Now, it is as well-confirmed as any tradition can be that Kapila sat in meditation for many years at Hardwar, also known as Gangadvara <note>original: *Gangâdvâra*, meaning "the door or gate of the Ganges"</note>, located at the foot of the Himalayas. Not far from the Siwalik range, the mountain pass of Hardwar is still called "Kapila's Pass" to this day, and the ascetics there call the place "Kapilasthen" <note>original: *Kapilasthen*, meaning "the place of Kapila"</note>. It is at this location that the Ganges River, emerging from its mountain gorge, begins its journey across the hot plains of India.

<summary>This page discusses the sage Kapila, founder of the Sankhya philosophy, and argues that the Puranic story of him destroying King Sagara's sons is a symbolic allegory for the purification of human passions. It also connects the legend to the geographical location of Hardwar in India.</summary>

<header>THE SECRET DOCTRINE.</header>

It has been clearly established by geological surveys that the tradition claiming the ocean once reached the base of the Himalayas ages ago is not entirely without foundation, as distinct traces of this still remain. The Sânkhya philosophy <note>one of the six major schools of Hindu philosophy, focused on the dualism of consciousness and matter</note> may have been *brought down* and taught by the first Kapila, and written down by the *last Kapila*.

To this day in India, "Sâgara" is the name used for the ocean, and especially for the Bay of Bengal at the mouth of the Ganges.* Have geologists ever calculated how many thousands of years it must have taken for the sea to recede to its current distance from Hardwar, which is now 1,024 feet above sea level? If they had, those scholars of the East who claim Kapila lived between the first and ninth centuries AD might change their opinions, for at least two very good reasons. First, the actual number of years that have passed since Kapila’s time is clearly recorded in the *Purânas* <note>ancient Indian texts documenting history, tradition, and mythology</note>, though translators may fail to recognize it. Second, the Kapila of the Satya Yuga <note>the first and most spiritual of the four world ages</note> and the Kapila of the Kali Yuga <note>the current "dark age" of spiritual and physical decline</note> may be the same *individuality* <note>the eternal soul</note>, without being the same *personality* <note>the specific physical incarnation</note>.

Kapila, besides being the name of a person—the once-living Sage and the author of the Sânkhya philosophy—is also the generic name for the Kumâras, the celestial Ascetics and Virgins. Therefore, the very fact that the *Bhâgavata Purâna* identifies that Kapila—whom it had just described as a portion of the god Vishnu—as the author of the Sânkhya philosophy should have warned the reader of a "blind" <note>a literary device used in esoteric writings to hide deeper truths from those not ready for them</note> containing a hidden meaning. Whether he was the son of Vitatha, as the *Harivamsha* claims, or of anyone else, the author of the Sânkhya cannot be the same as the Sage of the Satya Yuga—the very beginning of the Manvantara <note>a vast period of time in Hindu cosmology; a "Day of Brahma"</note>—when Vishnu is *shown in the form of Kapila*, "imparting true Wisdom to all creatures." This refers to that ancient period when the "Sons of God" taught newly created humanity the arts and sciences, which have since been cultivated and preserved in secret sanctuaries by the Initiates. There are several well-known Kapilas in the *Purânas*: first the primeval Sage; then Kapila, one of the three "secret" Kumâras; and Kapila, the son of Kashyapa and Kadrû—the "many-headed serpent"†—in addition to Kapila the great Sage and Philosopher of the Kali Yuga. The latter, being an Initiate, a "Serpent of Wisdom," or a Nâga <note>a semi-divine being, often synonymous with an advanced spiritual teacher or "Serpent of Wisdom"</note>, was intentionally blended with the Kapilas of previous ages.

### SECTION X.
### THE CROSS AND THE PYTHAGOREAN DECAD.

---

The early Gnostics claimed that their <term>Science</term>, the <term>Gnosis</term> <note>original: "Gnosis," referring to direct spiritual knowledge or insight</note>, rested on a square, the angles of which represented respectively <term>Sigê</term> (Silence), <term>Bythos</term> (Depth), <term>Nous</term> (Spiritual Soul or Mind), and <term>Aletheia</term> (Truth). It was they who were the first to reveal to the world what had remained concealed for ages: namely, the <term>Tau</term> <note>the T-shaped cross</note>, in the shape of a <term>Procrustean bed</term> <note>a reference to the Greek myth of Procrustes; here it symbolizes the material world or physical body that limits the soul</note>, and the "Christos" (the divine Spirit) as incarnating in the "Chrestos" (the human disciple or "good man"). This refers to the one who, for certain purposes, became a willing candidate for a series of mental and physical tortures.

For them, the whole of the <term>Universe</term>, both metaphysical and material, was contained within and could be expressed and described by the digits contained in the number 10, the <term>Pythagorean Decad</term>.

This <term>Decad</term>, representing the <term>Universe</term> and its evolution out of <term>Silence</term> and the <term>Unknown Depths of the Spiritual Soul</term>, or the <term>World Soul</term> <note>original Latin: "Anima Mundi"</note>, presented two sides or aspects to the student. It could be—and was at first—applied to the <term>Macrocosm</term> (the universe as a whole), after which it descended to the <term>Microcosm</term>, or man. There was, then, the purely intellectual and metaphysical, or the "Inner Science," and the just as purely materialistic or "surface science," both of which could be explained by and contained in the <term>Decad</term>. In short, it could be studied both by the deductive method of <term>Plato</term> and the inductive method of <term>Aristotle</term>. 

The former started from a <term>divine comprehension</term>, where <term>plurality</term> proceeded from <term>unity</term>—that is, the digits of the <term>Decad</term> appeared, only to be finally reabsorbed and lost in the <term>infinite Circle</term>. The latter depended on sensory perception alone, where the <term>Decad</term> could be regarded either as the <term>unity</term> that multiplies or as matter which differentiates. Its study was limited to the <term>plane surface</term>, to the <term>cross</term>, or the *seven* which proceeds from the *ten* (the perfect number) on Earth as in Heaven.

This dual system was brought, together with the <term>Decad</term>, by <term>Pythagoras</term> from <term>India</term>. It was the same system held by the <term>Brahmans</term> <note>original: "Brachmans"</note> and <term>Iranians</term>, as...

That they are called this by the ancient Greek philosophers is confirmed for us by the entire range of Sanskrit literature, such as the *Puranas* and the *Laws of Manu*. In these "Laws" or *Ordinances of Manu*, it is said that <term>Brahma</term> <note>the creator god in the Hindu Trimurti</note> first creates the "**ten Lords of Being**," the ten <term>Prajapati</term> or Creative Forces. These ten produce *seven* other <term>Manus</term>—or, as some manuscripts suggest, *Munin* (instead of *Manun*), meaning "**devotees**" or holy beings. These are the equivalent of the "seven Angels of the Presence" in Western religion. 

This mysterious number seven is born from the upper Triangle <image-desc>a small equilateral triangle symbol</image-desc>. This triangle itself arises from its own peak, or from the "Silent Depths" of the Unknown Universal Soul (<term>Sige</term> and <term>Bythos</term> <note>original Greek: *Sige* (Silence) and *Bythos* (Depth)</note>). This seven is the ***seven-leaf Saptaparna plant*** <note>original Sanskrit: *Saptaparna*, a tree often used in occult symbolism to represent the sevenfold nature of man</note>, which grows and reveals itself on the surface of the "soil of mystery" from a ***threefold root*** buried deep beneath that impenetrable ground. This idea is fully explained in Volume I, Part II, Section III, "Primordial Substance and Divine Thought." The reader should examine that section carefully to understand the metaphysical idea behind this symbol. 

In both humanity and nature, according to the "Cis-Himalayan" <note>referring to the region on this side of the Himalayas, often used by Blavatsky to denote her specific line of esoteric teaching</note> Esoteric Philosophy—which matches the cosmogony of the original Manu—Nature herself intends a sevenfold (septenary) division. Strictly speaking, only the seventh principle (<term>Purusha</term> <note>the cosmic man or pure consciousness</note>) is the Divine ***Self***. As stated in the *Laws of Manu*: "He [Brahma], having pervaded the subtle parts of those six beings of immeasurable brightness,"* created or summoned them to "***Self***-consciousness," or the awareness of that One ***Self***. Of these six, five elements (or principles, known as <term>Tattvas</term> <note>the basic elements or "realities" of nature</note> according to the commentator Medhatithi) "are called the ***atomic, perishable elements***"†; these are described in the section mentioned above.‡

We must now discuss the "mystery language" used by prehistoric races. It is not a phonetic language based on sounds, but a purely pictorial and symbolic tongue. Today, its full meaning is known only to a very few people; for the general public, it has been a completely dead language for over 5,000 years. However, most learned Gnostics, Greeks, and Jews were familiar with it and used it, though in very different ways. A few examples can be given.

On the higher plane of existence, number is not a digit but a zero—a circle. On the plane below, it becomes ***one***, which is an odd number. Each letter of the ancient alphabets had its own philosophical meaning and reason for being <note>original French: *raison d'être*</note>. Therefore, "Father Zeus" <note>original: *Pater Zeus* or *Πατὴρ Δεύς*</note> had nothing sexual or phallic in either its sound or the shape of its letters—at least according to the scholar Ragon.* If we turn now to the Hebrew alphabet, we find that while ***one*** or *Aleph* (א) is symbolized by a bull or an ox, ***ten***—the perfect number, or the ***One of the Kabbalah***—is a *Yod* (י, y, i, or j). As the first letter of "Jehovah," it represents the reproductive organ and other related concepts.

The odd numbers are considered divine, while the ***even*** numbers are terrestrial, devilish, and unlucky. The <term>Pythagoreans</term> <note>followers of the Greek philosopher Pythagoras</note> hated the "Binary" <note>the number two</note>. To them, it was the origin of differentiation—and therefore the origin of contrast, discord, or matter; the very beginning of evil. In the <term>Valentinian</term> system of the gods <note>a Gnostic tradition founded by Valentinus</note>, "Depth" and "Silence" <note>original: *Bythos* and *Sigê* (Chaos and Matter born in Silence)</note> are the primary Binary pair. Among the early Pythagoreans, however, the "Duad" <note>the number two</note> was that imperfect state into which the first manifested being fell when it became detached from the "Monad" <note>the One</note>. It was the point from which the two roads—the good and the evil—branched off. Anything that was double-faced or false was called "binary" by them. Only the number "One" was good and harmonious, because no disharmony can come from "One" alone. This is the origin of the Latin word *Solus* <note>meaning "alone" or "only"</note> in relation to the "One and Only God," the "Unknown" mentioned by the Apostle Paul. *Solus*, however, very soon evolved into *Sol*—the Sun.

The "Ternary" <note>the number three</note> is the first of the odd numbers, just as the triangle is the first of the geometric figures.† This number is truly the number of mystery *above all others*. To study it on a public level, one must read Ragon's *Philosophical and Interpretive Course of Initiations* <note>original: *Cours Philosophique et Interprétatif des Initiations*</note>. For its hidden or "esoteric" meaning, one must look to the Hindu symbolism of numerals, for the combinations applied to it are countless. It is upon the hidden properties of the three equal sides of the triangle that Ragon based his studies and founded the famous Masonic Society of the "Trinosophists"—those who study ***three sciences***. This was an improvement upon the ordinary three Masonic degrees, which were often given to those who studied nothing except eating and drinking at their Lodge meetings. As the founder writes:

-># THE MYSTIC MEANING OF MAKARA.<-

->609<-

Everyone knows that **Capricorn** (represented by the symbol ♑︎) is the tenth sign of the Zodiac, which the Sun enters at the winter solstice around December 21st. However, very few people—even in India, unless they have been initiated into sacred knowledge—know the real mystical connection that exists between the names **Makara** and **Kumâra**. 

The first term, *Makara*, refers to an amphibious animal that some <term>Orientalists</term> <note>scholars of Eastern languages and cultures</note> flippantly call a "crocodile." The second term, *Kumâra*, is the title given to the great patrons of <term>Yogis</term> <note>practitioners of yoga and meditation</note> according to the <term>Shaiva Purânas</term> <note>ancient Hindu texts dedicated to the god Shiva</note>. These beings are the sons of, and essentially one with, **Rudra** (Shiva), who is himself a Kumâra. It is through their connection with humanity that the Kumâras are also linked to the Zodiac. Let us try to discover what the word *Makara* truly means. The author of "The Twelve Signs of the Zodiac" states:

> Makara . . . contains within itself the clue to its correct interpretation. The letter *ma* is equivalent to the number 5, and *kara* means hand. Now, in Sanskrit, *Tribhujam* means a triangle—*bhujam* or *karam* (which are synonyms) being understood to mean a "side." Therefore, *Makaram* or *Panchakaram* means a Pentagon. <note>original: "Op. cit."; meaning: in the work previously cited, p. 113</note>

The five-pointed star, or pentagon, represents the five limbs of man. <note>What is the meaning and reason for this figure? The reason is that **Manas** (the mind) is the *fifth* principle of human nature, and the Pentagon is the symbol of Man—not just a physical body with five limbs, but rather the *thinking, conscious Man*.</note> We are told that under the ancient system, Makara was the *eighth* sign instead of the tenth. <note>The reason for this becomes clear when Egyptian symbolism is studied. See further on.</note>

> The sign in question is intended to represent the "faces" of the universe, and indicates that the structure of the universe is bounded by Pentagons. <note>original: "Ibid."; meaning: in the same place, p. 114</note>

Sanskrit writers "speak also of *Ashtadisha*, or eight faces bounding Space," referring to the **Loka-pâlas**—the eight points of the compass (the four cardinal and four intermediate points).

> From a physical perspective, the "microcosm" <note>the "little world," or man</note> is represented by the human body. *Makaram* may be taken to represent simultaneously both the microcosm and the macrocosm <note>the "great world," or universe</note> as external objects of perception. <note>original: "Ibid."; meaning: in the same place, pp. 114, 115</note>

However, the true <term>Esoteric</term> <note>hidden or inner</note> meaning of the word *Makara* is not actually "crocodile" at all, even when compared to the animal depicted on the Hindu Zodiac. In that context, it has the head and forelegs of an **antelope** and the body and tail of a **fish**. Consequently, the tenth sign of the Zodiac has been interpreted variously as a shark, a dolphin, and so on. It is the **Vâhana** <note>the divine vehicle or mount</note> of **Varuna**, the God of the Ocean.

In these beings, Water and <term>Ether</term> <note>the spiritual substance filling space</note> predominate; therefore, their symbols were both *aquatic* and *fiery*.

Wisdom lies hidden under the couch of the one who rests on the Golden <term>Lotus</term> <note>original: "Padma"</note> floating on the Water.

In India, this being is <term>Vishnu</term>; one of his <term>Avatars</term> <note>original: "Avatâras"; divine incarnations</note> was the Buddha, as was claimed in ancient times. The <term>Prachetasas</term> <note>a group of ten (or five) legendary sages</note>, the worshippers of <term>Narayana</term>—who, like Poseidon, moved or lived *over* the waters rather than under them—plunged into the depths of the Ocean for their devotions and remained there for 10,000 years. The Prachetasas are *ten* in public teachings, but *five* in secret, <term>Esoteric</term> <note>intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge</note> teachings. In Sanskrit, <term>Prachetâs</term> is a name for <term>Varuna</term>, the Water God, also known as <term>Nereus</term>, an aspect of Neptune. Thus, the Prachetasas are identical to the "five ministers" of the male-female <term>Chozzar</term> <note>original: "Χωζζάρ or Χορζάρ"</note>, or Poseidon, mentioned by the <term>Peratae Gnostics</term> <note>an early mystical Christian group</note>. These ministers are respectively called Ou, Aoai, Ouô, Ouôab <note>original: "Οὐ, Ἀοαί, Οὐώ, Οὐώαβ"</note>, and . . . . the *fifth*, which has a triple name (making seven in total), is lost†—that is, kept secret. This explains the "aquatic" symbol. Their "fiery" aspect connects them to spiritual symbols of fire. To help identify them, remember that just as the mother of the Prachetasas was <term>Savarna</term>, the daughter of the Ocean, so was <term>Amphitrite</term> the mother of Neptune's mystic "ministers."

The reader is reminded that these "five ministers" are symbolized both by the Dolphin—who overcame the chaste Amphitrite’s refusal to marry Poseidon—and by their son, <term>Triton</term>. Triton, whose body is a man above the waist and a dolphin or fish below, is mysteriously connected to <term>Oannes</term> (the Babylonian Fish-god <term>Dag</term>) and also to the <term>Fish</term> <note>original: "Matsya"</note> Avatar of Vishnu; both figures taught Wisdom to mortals. As every mythologist knows, Poseidon placed the Dolphin among the constellations as a reward for its service. To the Greeks, this became <term>Capricorn</term> <note>original: "Capricornus"</note>, the Goat, whose hind part is that of a dolphin. This makes it identical to the <term>Makara</term>, a creature with the head of an antelope and the body and tail of a fish. This is why the sign of the Makara was carried on the banner of <term>Kamadeva</term>, the Hindu God of Love. In the *Atharva Veda*, Kamadeva is identified with <term>Agni</term>, the Fire-god, and described as the son of <term>Lakshmi</term>, as correctly stated in the *Harivamsa*. This is because Lakshmi and Venus are the same deity, and Amphitrite is an early form of Venus. Now <term>Kama</term>, who carries the Makara on his banner, is also called <term>Aja</term>, the "un-

# THE PUZZLES OF SYMBOLISM.

The <term>Dhyân Chohans</term> <note>celestial beings or "lords of meditation"</note>, called <term>Kumâras</term> <note>the "ever-virgin" youthful sages</note> in India, are connected with both light and darkness. Moreover, in the <term>exoteric</term> <note>public or outward</note> religions, they have become synonymous with the "Angels of Darkness." <term>Mâra</term> <note>the personification of temptation and death in Buddhism</note> is the God of Darkness, the Fallen One, and Death;* and yet it is one of the names of <term>Kâma</term> <note>Desire</note>, the First God in the <term>Vedas</term> <note>ancient Hindu scriptures</note>, the <term>Logos</term> <note>the first manifestation of divine reason</note>, from whom the Kumâras have sprung. This connects them even more closely with our "fabulous" Indian <term>Makara</term> <note>a mythical sea-creature, often depicted as a crocodile or dragon</note> and the crocodile-headed God in Egypt.† The Crocodiles in the Celestial Nile are *five*, and the God Toom—the Primordial Deity who creates the heavenly bodies and living beings—calls forth these Crocodiles in his *fifth* "creation." When Osiris, the "Deceased Sun," is buried and enters into <term>Amenti</term> <note>the Egyptian underworld</note>, the sacred Crocodiles plunge into the abyss of primordial Waters—the "Great Green One." When the Sun of Life rises, they re-emerge out of the sacred river. All of this is highly symbolic and shows how primeval esoteric truths found expression in identical symbols across cultures. But, as Mr. T. Subba Row truly declares:

> The veil that was skillfully thrown over certain portions of the mystery connected with these Zodiacal signs by the ancient philosophers will never be lifted *for the amusement or instruction of the uninitiated public.*‡

Nor was the number five any less sacred to the Greeks. The "Five Words" of Brahmâ became, with the <term>Gnostics</term> <note>early Christian mystics who emphasized secret knowledge</note>, the "Five Words" written upon the <term>Âkâshic</term> <note>shining or ethereal</note> Garment of Jesus at his glorification. These words—"Zama Zama Ôzza Rachama Ôzai" (ΖΑΜΑ ΖΑΜΑ ΩΖΖΑ ΡΑΧΑΜΑ ΩΖΑΙ)—were translated by Orientalists as "the robe, the glorious robe of my strength." These words were, in turn, an anagrammatic <term>blind</term> <note>a symbolic veil used to hide a deeper secret</note> for the five mystic Powers represented on the robe of the "resurrected" Initiate after his final trial of a three-day trance. The five become *seven* only after his "death," when the <term>Adept</term> <note>a master of esoteric knowledge</note> became the full <term>Christos</term>, the full Krishna-Vishnu—that is, merged into <term>Nirvâna</term>. The <term>E Delphicum</term> <note>the letter "E" displayed at the Temple of Delphi</note>, a sacred symbol, was also the numeral *five*. How sacred it was is shown by the fact that the Corinthians, according to Plutarch, replaced the wooden numeral in the Delphic Temple with a bronze one, and this was later transformed by Livia Augusta into a replica made of gold.§

The Six, or the <term>Senary</term> <note>a set of six</note>, is dealt with later in this section, while the <term>Septenary</term> <note>a set of seven</note> will be fully treated in the course of this volume in the section on “The Mysteries of the <term>Hebdomad</term>” <note>from the Greek word for seven</note>.

The <term>Ogdoad</term> <note>a set of eight</note>, or the number eight, symbolizes the eternal and spiral motion of cycles (represented by the figure 8 or the infinity symbol ∞) and is symbolized in its turn by the <term>Caduceus</term> <note>the winged staff of Hermes, featuring two snakes entwined around it</note>. Then comes the number nine, or the triple <term>Ternary</term> <note>a group of three</note>. It is the number which reproduces itself incessantly under all shapes and figures in every multiplication. It is the sign of every circumference, since its value in degrees is equal to 9 (that is, 3 + 6 + 0 = 9). It is a *bad* number under certain conditions and very unlucky. If the number 6 was the symbol of our Globe ready to be animated by a *divine Spirit*, then 9 symbolized our Earth inhabited by a *bad or evil Spirit*.

Ten, or the <term>Decad</term> <note>a set of ten</note>, brings all these digits back to unity and ends the <term>Pythagorean table</term> <note>the basic system of numbers from 1 to 10 used by the followers of Pythagoras</note>. If we now turn our attention to the Egyptian cross, or the <term>Tau</term> <note>the letter 'T'</note>, we may discover this letter—which was so highly honored by Egyptians, Greeks, and Jews—to be mysteriously connected with the Decad. The Tau is the Alpha and the Omega <note>original: "Alpha and Omega"—the first and the last</note> of Secret Divine Wisdom, which is symbolized by the initial and the final letters of Thot (Hermes). Thot was the inventor of the Egyptian alphabet, and the letter Tau closed the alphabets of the Jews and the Samaritans, who called this character the “end” or “perfection,” “culmination,” and “security.” Hence, Ragon tells us, the words *Terminus* <note>Latin: "end"</note> and *Tectum* <note>Latin: "roof"</note> are symbols of shelter and security—which is a rather mundane definition. # THE "GOLDEN CANDLESTICK."

...piped flute <note>This likely refers to the seven-piped "pan flute" of the god Pan, mentioned on the previous page</note>, the emblem of the seven forces of Nature, the seven planets, the seven musical notes, and, in short, all seven-fold harmony, clearly shows his primal character. The same is true of the cross. Long before the Jews designed the golden candlestick for their Temple—with *three* sockets on one side and *four* on the other, turning the number *seven* into a feminine number of reproduction\* (and thus introducing a <term>phallic</term> <note>relating to the generative or sexual organs as symbols of nature's power</note> element into religion)—more spiritually-minded nations had already made the cross (represented by 3 + 4 = 7) their most sacred divine symbol. In fact, the circle, the cross, and the number seven—the latter being used as a basis for *measuring circles*—are the earliest primal symbols. <term>Pythagoras</term> <note>a Greek philosopher and mathematician whose teachings emphasized the mystical power of numbers</note>, who brought his wisdom from India, left to future generations a glimpse into this truth. His school of thought regarded the number 7 as a combination of the numbers 3 and 4, which they explained in two ways. On the level of the spiritual <term>noumenal</term> <note>the world of ideas or things-in-themselves, as opposed to how they appear to our senses</note> world, the Triangle was the first concept of the revealed God, representing the image of "Father-Mother-Son." Meanwhile, the <term>Quaternary</term> <note>the number four</note>, the perfect number, was the spiritual, ideal root of all numbers and objects on the physical plane. 

Some students, because of the holiness of the <term>Tetraktys</term> <note>a triangular figure consisting of ten points arranged in four rows, sacred to the Pythagoreans</note> and the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>the four-letter Hebrew name of God, usually transliterated as YHWH</note>, misunderstand the mystical meaning of the Quaternary. For the ancients, the number four was only a secondary "perfection," so to speak, because it only related to the physical world. Instead, it is the Triangle—the Greek letter <term>Delta</term> ($\Delta$)—which was the "vehicle of the unknown God." Strong evidence for this is found in the fact that the name of God often begins with the letter Delta. The name Zeus was written as *Deus* <note>original: $\Delta\epsilon\acute{\upsilon}\varsigma$</note> by the Boeotians, which led to the Latin word *Deus* <note>the Latin word for God</note>. 

This explains the metaphysical concept regarding the meaning of the seven-fold system in the *perceived world*; however, for the purposes of common or public interpretation, the symbolism changed. Three became the symbol for the three *material elements*—Air, Water, and Earth—while *four* became the principle for everything that is neither physical nor detectable by the senses. But true Pythagoreans never accepted this view. When seen as a combination of 6 and 1—the <term>Senary</term> <note>a set of six</note> and Unity—the number 7 was the invisible center, the Spirit of everything, as there exists no—

# THE ROOT OF WISDOM.

According to the same scholar, Osiris represented the Sun, the river Nile, and the solar year of 365 days. Isis, on the other hand, represented the Moon, the bed of that river, or Mother Earth—"for whose life-giving <note>original: "parturient"</note> energies water was a necessity"—as well as the lunar year of 354 days, "the time-keeper of the periods of pregnancy <note>original: "gestation"</note>." All of this is interpreted as sexual and <term>phallic</term> <note>relating to or representing the male generative organ as a symbol of creative power</note>; modern scholars seem to find nothing in these symbols beyond a physiological or sexual meaning. Nevertheless, the three digits 365 (the number of days in a solar year) only need to be interpreted with the Pythagorean key to reveal a highly philosophical and moral meaning. One instance will be sufficient. It can be read as:

->The Earth (3)—animated by (6)—the Spirit of Life (5).<-

This is simply because 3 is equivalent to the Greek letter Gamma (Γ), which is the symbol of Gaia (the Earth), while the figure 6 is the symbol of the animating or informing principle. The 5 represents the universal <term>quintessence</term> <note>the "fifth element" or pure essence that was thought to fill the universe beyond the four terrestrial elements</note> which spreads in every direction and forms all matter.*

The few instances and examples brought forward reveal only one small portion of the methods used to read the symbolic <term>ideographs</term> <note>characters or symbols representing ideas or things</note> and numerals of antiquity. Because the system is extremely complex and difficult, very few—even among the <term>Initiates</term> <note>those admitted into secret or sacred knowledge</note>—could master all seven keys of interpretation. Is it any wonder, then, that the metaphysical meaning gradually declined into a study of physical nature? The Sun, which was once the symbol of God <note>original: "Deity"</note>, became—as long ages <note>original: "æons"</note> glided by—merely a symbol of its creative heat <note>original: "ardour"</note>, and from there it fell into a symbol of phallic significance. But surely those who followed Plato’s method—proceeding from universal truths down to specific details—would never have begun by using sexual emblems to symbolize their religions! It is quite true, as stated by that living contradiction Éliphas Lévi <note>a famous 19th-century French occultist</note>, that "man is God on Earth, and God is man in Heaven." But this could not, and never did, apply to the One God; it applied only to the groups <note>original: "Hosts"</note> of Its incarnated beams, which we call <term>Dhyân Chohans</term> <note>Sanskrit for "Lords of Meditation," high-ranking celestial beings</note>. The Ancients called them Gods, but the Church has now transformed them into Devils on the *left* side, and into the Saviour on the *right* side!

But all such dogmas grew out of the same source: the root of Wisdom, which grows and thrives on Indian soil. There is not an Archangel that cannot be traced back to its prototype in the sacred land of <term>Âryâvarta</term> <note>an ancient Sanskrit name for Northern India</note>. These prototypes are all connected with the <term>Kumâras</term> <note>in Hindu thought, the "mind-born" sons of Brahma who remained pure and refused to create physical offspring</note> who appear on the scene of action by "refusing"—as Sanatkumâra and Sananda did—to "create progeny." Yet they are called the "creators"...

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

These entities are associated with (thinking) man. More than once they are connected with Nârada—another collection of *seeming contradictions*, yet a wealth of philosophical principles. Nârada is the leader of the Gandharvas, the celestial singers and musicians. From an esoteric perspective, the reason for this is explained by the fact that the Gandharvas are "the instructors of men in the Secret Sciences." It is they who, "loving the women of the Earth," revealed to them the mysteries of creation; or, as in the *Veda*, the "heavenly" Gandharva is a deity who knew and revealed the secrets of heaven and divine truths in general. If we remember what is said of this class of Angels in the *Book of Enoch* and in the *Bible*, then the allegory is plain: their leader, Nârada, while refusing to produce offspring <note>original: "procreate"</note>, leads men to become Gods. 

Moreover, as stated in the *Vedas*, all of these are Chhandajas—"will-born," or incarnated in different <term>Manvantaras</term> <note>great cycles of time in Hindu cosmology</note> by their *own will*. They are shown in <term>exoteric</term> <note>public or literal</note> literature as existing age after age; some being "sentenced to be reborn," while others incarnate as a duty. Finally, as the Sanakadikas—the seven Kumâras who went to visit Vishnu on the "White Island" (*Shveta-dvîpa*), the island inhabited by the Great Yogis <note>original: "Mahâ Yogins"</note>—they are connected with *Shâka-dvîpa* and the Lemurians and Atlanteans of the Third and Fourth Root Races.

In the Esoteric Philosophy, the Rudras (including the Kumâras, Âdityas, Gandharvas, Asuras, etc.) are the highest Dhyân Chohans or <term>Devas</term> <note>divine beings or gods</note> in terms of intellect. They are those who, because they acquired a *five-fold nature* through self-development—which is why the number *five* is sacred—became independent of the pure *Arûpa* <note>formless</note> Devas. This is a mystery that is very difficult to perceive and understand correctly. For we see that those who were "obedient to law" are, equally with the "rebels," *destined to be reborn in every age*. 

Nârada, the <term>Rishi</term> <note>an inspired poet or sage</note>, is cursed by Brahmâ to constant wandering <note>original: "peripateticism"</note> on Earth—that is <note>original: "i.e."</note>, to be constantly reborn. He is a rebel against Brahmâ, and yet he has no worse fate than the Jayas—the twelve great Creative Gods produced by Brahmâ as his assistants in the work of creation. These latter gods, lost in meditation, simply *forgot to create*; for this, they were equally cursed by Brahmâ to be born in every Manvantara. And still, they are called—along with the rebels—Chhandajas, or those born of their own will in human form.

# THE HOSTS OF THE BLESSED ONES.

Western scholars of Eastern cultures <note>original: "Orientalists"</note> refuse to be confused by these complexities. They solve the difficult problem <note>original: "cutting the Gordian knot"</note> by simply declaring the entire system to be "figments... of Brahmanical imagination and a love of exaggeration." But to the student of the hidden sciences <note>original: "Occultism"</note>, the whole system is full of deep philosophical meaning. We are happy to leave the superficial "rind" to the Western experts in Sanskrit, but we claim the inner essence of the knowledge for ourselves. We go further: we admit that, in one sense, much of what is found in these so-called "fables" refers to astronomical metaphors <note>original: "allegories"</note> regarding constellations, star clusters <note>original: "asterisms"</note>, stars, and planets. Yet, while the Gandharva <note>celestial musicians and keepers of the soma in Hindu mythology</note> of the *Rig Veda* may be used there to represent the fire of the Sun, the Gandharva Devas are actually beings with both a physical and psychological nature. Similarly, the Apsarasas <note>celestial nymphs</note> (along with other *Rudras*) represent both abstract qualities and measurable quantities. In short, if ever fully understood, the genealogy of the Vedic gods <note>original: "Theogony"</note> will reveal the deep mysteries of creation and existence. As the sage Parâshara truly says:

> These classes of thirty-three divinities . . . exist age after age, and their appearance and disappearance happens in the same way that the sun sets and rises again.\*

There was once a time when the Eastern symbol of the cross within a circle, the *Svastika* <note>The Swastika is an ancient symbol of peace and continuity, used globally for millennia before its 20th-century misappropriation</note>, was universally adopted. To the inner-circle <note>original: "Esoteric"</note> and even the public <note>original: "exoteric"</note> Buddhist, the Chinese, and the Mongolian, it represents the "ten thousand truths." These truths, they say, belong to the mysteries of the invisible universe and the primary origins of the cosmos and the gods.

*Since Fohat <note>The personified electrical vital power; the messenger of the gods</note> crossed the Circle like two lines of flame* <note>[horizontally and vertically]</note>, *the Hosts of the Blessed Ones have never failed to send their representatives to the planets they have been appointed to watch over since the beginning.*

This is why the *Svastika*—much like the "handled cross" <note>original: "ansated cross" or Ankh</note> was in Egypt—is always placed on the chest of deceased Mystics. It is found over the heart of images and statues of Buddha in Tibet and Mongolia. It is also a seal placed on the hearts of living Initiates, and for some, it is even permanently branded into the flesh. This is because they must keep these truths pure and unchanged, in eternal silence and secrecy, until the day they are recognized and read by their chosen successors—new Initiates who are "worthy of being entrusted with the ten thousand perfections." However, the symbol has become so degraded today that it is often found on the headdresses of "gods"—the ugly idols of the disrespectful Bhons (the *Dugpas* or sorcerers of the Tibetan borderlands)—until they are discovered by a *Gelugpa* <note>original: "Galukpa"; a member of the "Yellow Hat" school of Tibetan Buddhism</note> and the symbol is torn off along with the idol's head.
