<header>THE SECRET DOCTRINE.</header>

Compare this to the Eastern School of Theosophy, and then decide which is more correct. Truly:

> Wisdom has built her house,
> She has carved out her *seven pillars.* <note>original: "Wisdom hath builded her house, She hath hewn out her seven pillars." — Proverbs 9:1</note>

As for the accusation that our School has not adopted the sevenfold classification of the Brahmans <note>priestly or scholarly caste in India</note> but has instead confused it, this is quite unjust. To begin with, the "School" itself is one thing, and its representatives to Europeans are quite another. The latter must first learn the basics of practical Eastern <term>Occultism</term> <note>the study of hidden spiritual laws and the inner nature of humanity</note> before they can correctly understand the tremendously complex classification based on the seven distinct states of **Prajñâ** <note>Sanskrit: supreme wisdom, insight, or consciousness</note>; and, above all, they must thoroughly realize what *Prajñâ* truly is in Eastern metaphysics. 

To provide a Western student with that classification is to lead them to believe they can explain the origin of consciousness simply by explaining the process by which a specific piece of knowledge—even though it is only *one* of the states of that consciousness—came to them. In other words, it is to ask them to account for something they know on *this physical plane* by using something they know nothing about on other planes. That is, it would lead them directly from the spiritual and psychological realms into <term>ontology</term> <note>the branch of philosophy dealing with the nature of being and existence</note>. This is why the primary, ancient classification was adopted by the Theosophists—and in truth, there are many such classifications.

After such a vast number of independent witnesses and proofs have been presented to the public, it would be quite useless to busy ourselves with additional lists from theological sources. The seven "deadly" sins and seven virtues of the Christian system are far less philosophical than even the seven liberal and the seven accursed sciences—or the seven arts of enchantment of the <term>Gnostics</term> <note>early mystical groups who emphasized direct spiritual knowledge over orthodox dogma</note>. One of these latter arts is now before the public, and it is full of danger for both the present and the future. Its modern name is **Hypnotism**. When used by scientific and ignorant materialists who do not understand the seven principles of human nature, it will soon become **Satanism** <note>here meaning the malevolent misuse of spiritual or mental powers</note> in the full sense of the word.

## SCIENCE AND THE SECRET DOCTRINE CONTRASTED.

### SECTION I.

### ARCHAIC, OR MODERN ANTHROPOLOGY?

Whenever the question of the origin of humanity is seriously presented to an unbiased, honest, and dedicated scientist, the answer is always: "We do not know." Jean Louis Armand de Quatrefages <note>original: "De Quatrefages" — a French biologist and anthropologist known for his work on human origins and his critique of Darwin's theories</note>, with his agnostic stance, is one such anthropologist.

This does not mean that other scientists are neither fair-minded nor honest; saying so would be unwise. However, it is estimated that 75 percent of European scientists are evolutionists. Are these representatives of modern thought all guilty of blatant misrepresentation of the facts? No one is claiming that—though there are a few very exceptional cases. However, scientists—driven by their anti-religious enthusiasm and despairing of any alternative theory to <term>Darwinism</term> <note>the theory of the evolution of species by natural selection</note> other than that of "special creation" <note>the belief that the universe and all life originated from specific divine acts</note>—are unconsciously insincere. They are "forcing" a hypothesis that is not flexible enough to support the weight they place on it, and it is showing the strain of being stretched too far.

Insincerity on this same subject is also evident in religious circles. Bishop Frederick Temple <note>later the Archbishop of Canterbury, who sought to reconcile Christian doctrine with evolution</note> has come forward as a thorough supporter of Darwinism in his work *Religion and Science*. This religious writer goes so far as to regard matter—after it has received its "initial push" <note>original: "primal impress"</note>—as the sole, unaided source of all cosmic phenomena. This view only differs from that of Ernst Haeckel <note>original: "Hæckel" — a German biologist and philosopher who promoted Darwinism in Germany</note> by suggesting a hypothetical Deity at "the back of beyond"—a Deity who stands entirely distant from the interaction of natural forces. Such a metaphysical entity is no more the Theo- <note>The text breaks off here at the end of the page, likely continuing to "Theos" or "Theological Deity."</note>

...logical God than is that of Kant <note>original: "Kant" — Immanuel Kant (1724–1804), the German philosopher who explored the limits of human reason and the necessity of belief in God for morality</note>. In the presence of this display of **flunkeyism** <note>servile or fawning behavior; acting like a servant</note> before the materialism of our "learned" age, we Occultists can only smile. But what about loyalty to the Master such theological runaways claim to serve—Christ and the Christian world at large?

However, we have no desire, for the present, to challenge the clergy; our business now is with materialistic science alone. The latter, represented by its best scholars, answers our question with, "We do not know." Yet the majority of them act as though **omniscience** <note>the state of knowing everything</note> were their birthright and they knew all things.

For, indeed, this admission of ignorance has not prevented the majority of scientists from speculating on the question, each seeking to have his own special theory accepted to the exclusion of all others. Thus, from Maillet in 1748 down to Haeckel in 1870, theories on the origin of the human race have differed as much as the personalities of their inventors themselves. Buffon, Bory de St. Vincent, Lamarck, E. Geoffroy St. Hilaire, Gaudry, Naudin, Wallace, Darwin, Owen, Haeckel, Filippi, Vogt, Huxley, Agassiz, etc. <note>This list includes the most prominent naturalists and evolutionary thinkers of the 18th and 19th centuries</note>, each has evolved a more or less scientific hypothesis of genesis. De Quatrefages <note>Jean Louis Armand de Quatrefages (1810–1892), a French biologist known for opposing the idea that humans descended from apes</note> arranges these theories into two principal groups—one based on a rapid transformation and the other on a very gradual **transmutation** <note>the change of one species into another</note>; the former favors a new type (humanity) produced by a being entirely different, while the latter teaches the evolution of humans by progressive changes.

Strangely enough, it is from the most scientific of these authorities that the most unscientific of all theories regarding the origin of man has emerged. This is now so evident that the hour is rapidly approaching when the current teaching about the descent of man from an ape-like mammal will be regarded with less respect than the formation of Adam out of clay and of Eve out of Adam’s rib. For:

> It is evident, especially according to the most fundamental principles of Darwinism, that an organized being cannot be a descendant of another whose development occurs in the opposite order to its own. Consequently, in accordance with these principles, man cannot be considered as the descendant of any ape-like type whatsoever.

# “PHYSIOLOGICAL” VERSUS “NATURAL” SELECTION.

Lucae’s <note>original: "Lucae" — Johann Christian Gustav Lucae (1814–1885), a German anatomist known for his studies on the cranium</note> argument against the Ape-theory—based on the different curvatures of the bones constituting the axis of the skull in humans and the great apes—is fairly discussed by Schmidt <note>original: "Schmidt" — Oscar Schmidt (1823–1886), a German zoologist and supporter of Darwinism</note>. He admits that:

> The ape, as it grows, becomes more animal-like; man . . . more human—

and seems, indeed, to hesitate a moment before he continues:

> This curvature of the cranial axis may, therefore, still be emphasized as a human characteristic, in contrast to the apes; the specific characteristic of an order can hardly be derived from it; and especially regarding the doctrine of descent, this circumstance seems in no way decisive.*

The writer is evidently quite unsettled by his own argument. He assures us that it eliminates any possibility of the modern apes having been the ancestors of humanity. But does it not also deny the bare possibility of humans and the great apes having had a common—though, so far, an absolutely theoretical—ancestor?

Even “Natural Selection” itself is becoming more threatened every day. The deserters from the Darwinian camp are many, and those who were at one time its most enthusiastic disciples are, due to new discoveries, slowly but steadily preparing to change their minds <note>original: "turn over a new leaf"</note>. In the *Journal of the Royal Microscopical Society* for October 1886, we may read as follows:

<term>PHYSIOLOGICAL SELECTION</term>.—Mr. G. J. Romanes <note>George John Romanes (1848–1894), an evolutionary biologist who sought to resolve certain gaps in Darwin's theory</note> finds certain difficulties in regarding natural selection as a theory for the origin of species, as it is rather a theory of the origin of adaptive structures. He proposes to replace it with what he calls "physiological selection," or the "segregation of the fit." His view is based on the extreme sensitivity of the reproductive system to small changes in life conditions, and he thinks that variations toward greater or lesser sterility must frequently occur in wild species. If the variation is such that the reproductive system, while showing some degree of sterility with the parent form, continues to be fertile within the limits of the new variety, the variation would neither be overwhelmed by cross-breeding nor die out on account of sterility. When a variation of this kind occurs, the physiological barrier must divide the species into two parts. The author, in short <note>original: "in fine"</note>, regards mutual sterility, not as one of the effects of species differentiation, but as the cause of it.†

An attempt is made to show the above to be a supplement to, and a consequence of, the Darwinian theory. This is a clumsy attempt at best.

->THE SECRET DOCTRINE.<-

The public will soon be asked to believe that Mr. C. Dixon's *Evolution without Natural Selection* is also Darwinism—expanded, as the author certainly claims it to be!

But this is like splitting a man’s body into three pieces and then maintaining that each piece is the identical man he was before, only "expanded." Yet the author states:

> Let it be clearly understood that not one single syllable in the preceding pages has been written in opposition to Darwin's theory of Natural Selection. All I have done is to explain *certain phenomena* . . . the more one studies Darwin's works, the more one is convinced of the truth of his hypothesis [! !].*

And before this, he alludes to:

> The overwhelming array of facts which Darwin gave in support of his hypothesis, and which triumphantly carried the theory of Natural Selection over all obstacles and objections.†

However, this does not prevent the learned author from overturning this theory just as "triumphantly," and from even openly calling his work *Evolution without Natural Selection*—or, in so many words, presenting Darwin's fundamental idea as having been smashed to pieces.

As for Natural Selection itself, a massive misconception prevails among many modern thinkers who silently accept the conclusions of Darwinism. It is, for instance, a mere rhetorical trick to credit Natural Selection with the power of originating species. Natural Selection is not an entity; it is merely a convenient phrase for describing the way that the survival of the fit and the removal of the unfit among organisms are brought about by the "Struggle for Existence." Every group of organisms tends to multiply beyond what their resources can support. This constant battle for life—the "struggle to obtain enough to eat and to escape being eaten," added to the conditions of the environment—makes a perpetual weeding out of the unfit necessary. The *elite* of any group, sorted out this way, reproduce the species and pass on their physical characteristics to their descendants. All useful variations are thus preserved, and a progressive improvement is achieved. 

But Natural Selection—in the writer's humble opinion, "Selection as a *Power*"—is in reality a complete myth, especially when it is used to explain the "Origin of Species." It is merely a descriptive term for the way "useful variations" are fixed <note>original: "stereotyped"</note> once they have already been produced. By itself, "it" can *produce* nothing; it only operates on the raw material presented to it. The real question at issue is: What cause—combined with other secondary causes—produced these variations?

### THE OCCULT AND THE MODERN DOCTRINES.

What produces the "variations" in the organisms themselves? Many of these secondary causes are purely physical—climatic, dietary, and so on. Very well. But beyond these secondary aspects of organic evolution, a deeper principle must be sought. The Materialist's <note>Materialist: one who believes that nothing exists except matter and its movements and modifications</note> concepts of "spontaneous variations" and "accidental divergencies" are self-contradictory terms in a universe defined by "Matter, Force, and *Necessity*." Simple variation of types, without the supervising presence of a quasi-intelligent impulse, is powerless to account for the incredible complexities and wonders of the human body, for instance. The insufficiency of the Darwinists' mechanical theory has been exposed at length by Dr. Von Hartmann, among other purely skeptical <note>original: "negative"</note> thinkers. It is an insult to the reader's intelligence to write, as Ernst Haeckel does, of *blind*, indifferent cells "arranging themselves into organs." The Esoteric <note>Esoteric: intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge</note> solution for the origin of animal species is provided elsewhere in this work.

Those purely secondary causes of differentiation—grouped under the headings of sexual selection, natural selection, climate, isolation, and others—mislead the Western Evolutionist. They offer no real explanation for the "where" or "how" of the "ancestral types" which served as the *starting point* for physical development. The truth is that the differentiating "causes" known to modern science only come into operation after the *physicalization of the primeval animal root-types out of the astral* <note>astral: in this context, the non-physical or "ethereal" blueprint that precedes physical matter</note>. Darwinism only meets Evolution at its midway point—that is to say, when astral evolution has given place to the play of the ordinary physical forces with which our present senses are familiar. 

But even here, the Darwinian theory, even with the "expansions" recently attempted, is inadequate to explain the facts. The cause underlying physiological variation in species—a cause to which all other laws are subordinate and secondary—is a subconscious intelligence pervading matter. This is ultimately traceable to a reflection of the Divine and Dhyân-Chohanic <note>Dhyân-Chohanic: relating to the Dhyân-Chohans, the "Lords of Light" or high-level celestial beings who act as the architects of the visible world</note> wisdom. A similar conclusion has been reached by the well-known thinker Eduard von Hartmann. Despairing of the efficacy of unaided Natural Selection, he regards Evolution as being intelligently guided by "the Unconscious"—the Cosmic Logos <note>Logos: the divine reason or creative word implicit in the cosmos</note> of Occultism. However, the latter acts only indirectly through Fohat <note>Fohat: the active, "running" force of cosmic electricity or vital energy that links spirit to matter</note>, or Dhyân-Chohanic energy, and not quite in the direct manner which the great pessimist describes.

It is this disagreement among scientists—their mutual and often *self-contradictory* views—that gives the writer of these volumes the courage to bring to light other and older teachings, even if only as hypotheses for *future* scientific evaluation. Even to the humble recorder of this ancient teaching, though she is not highly learned in modern sciences, the scientific errors and gaps are so obvious that she has determined to address them all in order to place the two sets of teachings side by side. Under these circumstances, the chances for an impartial hearing of the doctrines of Archaic Wisdom are few indeed. The educated public is told that:

# “THE TESTIMONY OF POVERTY <note>original: *testimonium paupertatis*</note> OF NATURAL SCIENCE.”

The social instincts of the lower animals have lately been regarded, for various reasons, as clearly being the origin of morals—even those of man [?]. . . . It is suggested that our divine consciousness, our soul, intellect, and aspirations have worked their “way up from the lower stages of the simple cell-soul” of the gelatinous Bathybius <note>original: "Bathybius." This refers to *Bathybius haeckelii*, a substance once thought by Ernst Haeckel and Thomas Huxley to be a primordial slime from which all life evolved; it was later proven to be merely a chemical precipitate of sulfate of lime.</note>—and they seem to believe it. For such men, the Metaphysics <note>metaphysics: the branch of philosophy dealing with the fundamental nature of reality, including the relationship between mind and matter</note> of Occultism <note>Occultism: the study of hidden spiritual knowledge or deeper realities beyond ordinary observation</note> must produce the same effect that our grandest oratorios produce on a person unaccustomed to Western music—sounds that jar upon their nerves.

Yet, are our Esoteric <note>Esoteric: intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge</note> teachings about “Angels,” the first three pre-animal human Races <note>In the author's system, these refer to early stages of human evolution that were spiritual and ethereal rather than physical.</note>, and the downfall of the Fourth <note>The "Fourth Race" refers to the Atlanteans, who the author claims fell into materialism and sin.</note>, *on a lower level of fiction and self-delusion* than the Haeckelian “plastidular” <note>Haeckel's term for a hypothetical "soul-unit" within a cell</note>, or the inorganic “molecular souls of the Protista <note>Protista: a kingdom of mostly single-celled organisms</note>”? Between the evolution of the spiritual nature of man from the above amoeba-like <note>original: "amœbian"</note> souls, and the alleged development of his physical frame from the protoplastic dweller in the ocean slime, there is an abyss which will not easily be crossed by any man in the *full* possession of his intellectual faculties. Physical Evolution, as Modern Science teaches it, is a subject for open controversy; spiritual and moral development on the same lines is the insane dream of a crass Materialism <note>Materialism: the theory that nothing exists except matter and its movements</note>.

Furthermore, past as well as present daily experience teaches that no truth has ever been accepted by learned bodies unless it has fit <note>original: "dove-tailed"</note> with the habitually preconceived ideas of their professors. “The crown of the innovator is a crown of thorns,” said Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire <note>Étienne Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire (1772–1844), a French naturalist who established the principle of "unity of composition."</note>. It is only that which fits in with popular hobbies and accepted notions that, as a general rule, gains ground. Hence the triumph of the Haeckelian ideas, notwithstanding that they are proclaimed by Virchow <note>Rudolf Virchow (1821–1902), a prominent German physician and pathologist who often disagreed with Haeckel's more extreme evolutionary views.</note>, du Bois-Reymond <note>Emil du Bois-Reymond (1818–1896), a German physician and physiologist.</note>, and others as the “*testimony of poverty* <note>original: *testimonium paupertatis*</note> of Natural Science.”

As diametrically opposed as the materialism of the German Evolutionists may be to the spiritual conceptions of Esoteric Philosophy, and as radically inconsistent as their accepted anthropological system is with the real facts of Nature—the pseudo-idealistic bias now coloring English thought is almost more harmful <note>original: "pernicious"</note>. The pure Materialistic Doctrine allows for a direct refutation and an appeal to the logic of facts. # READY-MADE MATERIALS OF SPEECH.

The fact is that only the partial truth of many of the secondary "laws" of Darwinism is beyond question. M. de Quatrefages evidently accepts natural selection, the struggle for existence, and transformation within species as proven only for the time being <note>original: *pro tempore*</note>, rather than once and for all. However, it may not be out of place to summarize the linguistic case against the "ape ancestor" theory:

Languages have their phases of growth, just like everything else in Nature. It is almost certain that the great families of language pass through three stages:

(1) All words are roots and are merely placed side-by-side (Radical languages).

(2) One root defines the other and becomes merely a modifying element (Agglutinative).

(3) The modifying element (the original meaning of which has long since faded) unites into a single whole with the main word (Inflected).

The problem then is: Where did these roots come from? Professor Max Müller argues that the existence of these *ready-made materials of speech* is proof that man cannot be the final result of a long biological series. This *potential to form roots* is the great difficulty which Materialists <note>those who believe that only physical matter exists and deny the spiritual or supernatural</note> almost always avoid.

# SCIENTIFIC TRESPASSERS.

<term>Haeckel</term> <note>Ernst Haeckel (1834–1919), a prominent German biologist and philosopher who championed Darwinism and proposed controversial theories on human evolution.</note> himself declares this repeatedly—therefore, in the eyes of exact research, their theories are no better or more reliable when extended into the remote past than are our Eastern Occult teachings; both must be placed on the same level. Furthermore, real scientists do not treat his <term>phylogenetic</term> <note>Relating to the evolutionary development and diversification of a species or group of organisms.</note> and <term>palingenetic</term> <note>The phase in the development of an individual organism that repeats the evolutionary history of its species.</note> speculations any more favorably than they do our theories regarding the cyclic repetitions of evolution in major and minor races, or our views on the original order of evolution. For the province of exact, real science—materialistic though it may be—is to carefully avoid anything resembling guesswork or unverifiable speculation. In short, it must avoid all suppression of the truth <note>original Latin: *suppressio veri*</note> and all suggestion of falsehood <note>original Latin: *suggestio falsi*</note>. 

The business of the man of exact science is to observe natural phenomena, each within his chosen department; to record, tabulate, compare, and classify facts down to the smallest details <note>original Latin: *minutiæ*</note> presented to the senses. This should be done with the help of the exquisite mechanisms provided by modern invention, not by the aid of metaphysical flights of fancy. The only legitimate right he has is to use physical instruments to correct the defects or illusions of his own coarser sight, hearing, and other senses. He has no right to trespass onto the grounds of <term>Metaphysics</term> <note>The branch of philosophy that deals with the first principles of things, including abstract concepts such as being, knowing, substance, cause, identity, time, and space.</note> and Psychology. His duty is to verify and correct all facts that fall under his direct observation and to profit from the experiences and mistakes of the past. He should endeavor to trace the workings of a specific chain of cause and effect which—only through constant and unvarying repetition—may be called a "Law." This is what a man of science is expected to do if he wishes to be a teacher of others and remain true to the original goals of the natural or physical sciences. Any detour from this main road becomes mere speculation.

Instead of sticking to this, what do many so-called men of science do today? They rush into the domain of pure Metaphysics while simultaneously mocking it. They delight in reaching rash conclusions and calling them "a deductive law derived from the inductive law" of a theory. These theories are drawn from the depths of their own consciousness—a consciousness that has been distorted and riddled by one-sided <term>Materialism</term> <note>The philosophical belief that nothing exists except matter and its movements and modifications.</note>. Such a scientist attempts to explain the "origin" of things that currently exist only within his own imagination. He attacks spiritual beliefs and religious traditions that are thousands of years old, denouncing everything as superstition except for his own pet theories. He proposes theories of the universe—a <term>cosmogony</term> <note>A theory or account of the origin and development of the universe.</note> developed by the blind, mechanical forces of nature alone—which are far more miraculous and impossible than even those based...

A "theory" is simply a hypothesis, a speculation, and *not a law*. To claim otherwise is one of the many liberties taken nowadays by scientists. They state an absurdity and then hide it behind the shield of Science. A deduction from theoretical speculation is nothing more than another theory.

In fact, in Darwin's theory, evolutionary changes <note>original: "transmutations"</note> do not take place either by chance or in every direction. They are ruled by certain laws that are due to the organization of the creature itself. It follows that two beings belonging to two distinct types can be referred to a ***common ancestor***, but one cannot be the descendant of the other.

# AN ABSOLUTELY THEORETICAL APE-LIKE MAN <note>original: "pithecoid man"</note>

These causes result in only slight embarrassment to Darwin. <note>Professor Oscar Schmidt, a supporter of Darwin, noted that Darwin's description of our early ancestors was "certainly not flattering, and perhaps in many points not correct."</note> We know that he considers the lack of information on similar questions as proof in his favor. THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

Haeckel himself divided mammals according to their anatomical differences into two groups: the *indeciduata*, which have no decidua (a special membrane uniting the placentas), and the *deciduata*, those who possess it. He includes the prosimians <note>original: "Prosimiæ," a group of primates including lemurs and lorises</note> in the latter group. Now we have shown elsewhere what other men of science had to say about this. As de Quatrefages <note>Jean Louis Armand de Quatrefages de Bréau, a French anthropologist</note> says:

> The anatomical investigations of... Milne Edwards and Grandidier upon these animals... place it beyond all doubt that the prosimians of Haeckel have no decidua and have a diffuse placenta. They are *indeciduata*. Far from any possibility of their being the ancestors of the apes, according to the principles laid down by Haeckel himself, they cannot even be regarded as the ancestors of the zonoplacental mammals <note>mammals characterized by a belt-shaped placenta</note>... and ought to be connected with the hoofed mammals (*Pachydermata*), the sloths and armadillos (*Edentata*), and the whales and dolphins (*Cetacea*).*

And yet Haeckel’s inventions pass with some as *exact science*!

The above mistake, if indeed it is one, is not even hinted at in Haeckel’s *Pedigree of Man*, translated by Aveling. If the excuse might be valid that at the time the famous “genealogies” were made, “the embryonic development of the prosimians was not known,” it is certainly familiar now. We shall see whether the next edition of Aveling’s translation will have this important error rectified, or if the seventeenth and eighteenth stages will remain as they are to blind the uninitiated <note>original: "profane"</note>, as if they were one of the *real* intermediate links. ### GEOLOGICAL FACTS BEARING ON THE QUESTION OF THEIR RELATIONSHIP.

The data derived from scientific research regarding "primeval man" and the ape provide no support for theories that humans descended from apes. "Where, then, must we look for primeval man?"—Huxley still asks, after having searched for him in vain in the very depths of the Quaternary <note>The most recent geological period, spanning the last 2.6 million years.</note> strata.

Was the oldest *Homo sapiens* <note>original: "wise man," the species name for modern humans</note> from the Pliocene or Miocene epochs, or even more ancient? In even older layers of earth, do the fossilized bones of an ape more human-like, or a man more ape-like <note>original: "pithecoid"</note> than any yet known, await discovery by some future paleontologist? Time will show.*

It certainly will—undeniably—and in doing so, it will vindicate the anthropology of the Occultists <note>Those who study hidden or esoteric spiritual knowledge.</note>. Meanwhile, in his eagerness to defend Darwin’s *Descent of Man*, Mr. Boyd Dawkins believes that he has nearly found the "missing link"—at least in theory. It was due to theologians more than geologists that, until nearly 1860, man had been considered a relic no older than the traditional 6,000 years associated with the biblical Adam. As Karma <note>The law of cause and effect; here used to mean "as fate would have it."</note> would have it, though, it was left to a French priest—Abbé Bourgeois—to give this comfortable theory an even worse blow than had been delivered by the discoveries of Boucher de Perthes <note>Jacques Boucher de Perthes (1788–1868) was one of the first to argue that humans existed alongside extinct animals based on stone tools he found.</note>. > They must either have been chipped by man, or, as Mr. Boyd Dawkins supposes, by the *dryopithecus* <note>An extinct genus of apes from the Miocene period.</note> or some other anthropoid ape. This ape would have needed a level of intelligence so much superior to the gorilla or chimpanzee as to be able to manufacture tools. But in this case, the problem would be solved and the missing link discovered, for such an ape might well have been the ancestor of Paleolithic <note>The "Old Stone Age," characterized by the earliest known stone tool use.</note> man.†

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

However, it is not so easy to see how this difference in physical structure began, or how a being came into existence with such a brain, such hands, and the latent potential for nearly unlimited progress. The problem is this: the structural difference between the lowest existing human race and the highest existing ape is too vast for one to be the direct descendant of the other. In some physical respects, Black people <note>original: "The negro"</note> were thought to slightly resemble the ape <note>original: "Simian"</note> type. Their skulls are narrower, their brains less capacious, their muzzles more projecting, and their arms longer than those of the average European. Yet they are still essentially human, separated by a wide gulf from the chimpanzee or the gorilla. Even someone with a severe developmental disability <note>original: "the idiot or crétin"</note>, whose brain size and intelligence are no greater than a chimpanzee’s, is a human with stunted development, not an ape.

Therefore, if Darwinian theory is correct regarding humans and apes, we must look back to a common ancestor from whom both originated. . . . But to prove this as a *fact* rather than a *theory*, we must find that ancestral form or, at the very least, intermediate stages leading toward it. . . in other words. . . the "missing link." Now it must be admitted that, so far, no such missing links have been discovered. Furthermore, the oldest known human skulls and skeletons—which date from the Ice Age <note>original: "Glacial period"</note> and are likely at least 100,000 years old—show no clear shift toward any such pre-human type. On the contrary, one of the oldest types—the people found in the burial cave <note>original: "sepulchral cave"</note> of Cro-Magnon*—belongs to a refined race: tall in stature, large in brain, and generally superior to many modern races of mankind.

The scientific response, of course, is that not enough time has passed. They argue that if humans and apes share an ancestor, and because highly developed apes certainly existed in the Miocene period <note>An epoch from about 23 to 5 million years ago</note> (and humans probably did too), that ancestor must be sought much further back—at a distance that makes the entire Quaternary period <note>The current geological period, beginning 2.6 million years ago</note> seem insignificant. . . . All this is true, and it should make us pause before concluding that humans are the only exception to the general laws of the universe, created through a unique act of "special creation." This is even harder to believe because the ape family, which humans so closely resemble [?] in physical structure, has many branches that blend into one another; yet the extremes of the ape family differ more from each other than humans differ from the highest apes. If a unique "special creation" is required for humans, would there not also need to be unique creations for the chimpanzee, the gorilla, the orangutan, and for at least 100 different species of apes and monkeys which are all built on the same anatomical lines? †

There *was* a "special creation" for humans, and a "special creation" for the ape—which is the human's *offspring* <note>original: "progeny"</note>—though this happened in a way Science has not yet considered. Albert Gaudry and others provide strong reasons why humans cannot be seen as the final evolution of an ape lineage. When one finds that not only was the "primeval savage" (?) a reality in the Miocene times, but that, as de Mortillet shows, the flint relics he has—

### "BLURRED COPIES" OF THEIR BESTIAL SIRES

The remnants left behind were splintered by *fire* in that remote epoch. # STATES OF CONSCIOUSNESS.

But there is even more to consider. The average person has no experience of any state of consciousness other than the one to which the physical senses connect him. How, then, while these mysteries remain unexplored, *can* we hope to speculate usefully on the nature of other Worlds which, in the natural order <note>original: "economy of Nature"</note>, must necessarily belong to states of consciousness that are completely different from *any* that humans experience here?

And this is literally true. For even great <term>Adepts</term> <note>highly advanced spiritual masters or initiates</note>—though they are trained <term>Seers</term> <note>individuals with developed spiritual or psychic vision</note>—can only claim to be thoroughly acquainted with the nature and appearance of planets and their inhabitants within our own Solar System. They *know* that almost all planetary worlds are inhabited, but—*even in spirit*—they can only access those within our system. 

They are also aware of how difficult it is, *even for them*, to put themselves into full connection <note>original: "rapport"</note> even with the planes of consciousness *within* our system, which differ so greatly from the states of consciousness possible on this globe. For instance, consider those that exist on the <term>Chain of Spheres</term> <note>in occult cosmology, a series of seven interconnected worlds or "globes" that life evolves through</note> on the three planes beyond our Earth. Such knowledge and interaction are possible for them because they have learned how to penetrate planes of consciousness that are closed to the perceptions of ordinary people. However, if they were to communicate their knowledge, the world would be no wiser; people lack the experience of other forms of perception that would allow them to grasp what they were being told.

Still, the fact remains that most planets, like the stars beyond our system, are inhabited—a fact that has been admitted by scientists themselves. Laplace and Herschel believed this, though they wisely avoided reckless speculation. The same conclusion has been developed and supported with a range of scientific arguments by Camille Flammarion, the well-known French astronomer. The arguments he presents are strictly scientific and appeal even to a materialistic mind, which would remain unmoved by the thoughts of someone like Sir David Brewster, the famous physicist, who writes:

> Those "barren spirits" or "base souls," as the poet calls them, who might be led to believe that the Earth is the only inhabited body in the universe, would have no difficulty in conceiving the Earth also to have been destitute of inhabitants. # THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

...admit that it was uninhabited for millions <note>original: "myriads"</note> of years; and here we arrive at the impossible conclusion that during these millions of years there was not a single intelligent creature in the vast domains of the Universal King <note>a reference to the Divine or the supreme governing principle of the universe</note>, and that before the <term>protozoic</term> <note>referring to the earliest geological age of life-forms</note> formations, there existed neither plant nor animal in all the infinity of space.*

Flammarion <note>Camille Flammarion (1842–1925), a famous French astronomer and author</note> shows, in addition, that all the conditions of life—even as *we* know it—are present on at least some of the planets, and points to the fact that these conditions must be much more favorable on them than they are on our Earth.

Thus, scientific reasoning, as well as observed facts, agrees with the statements of the <term>Seer</term> <note>a person with spiritual insight into the unseen</note> and the innate voice in man’s own heart in declaring that life—intelligent, conscious life—*must* exist on other worlds than ours.

But this is the limit beyond which the ordinary faculties of man cannot carry him. Many are the romances and tales—some purely fanciful, others bristling with scientific knowledge—which have attempted to imagine and describe life on other globes. But one and all, they give only a distorted copy of the drama of life around us. It is either, as with Voltaire <note>the French Enlightenment satirist</note>, the people of our own race seen under a microscope, or, as with Cyrano de Bergerac <note>French author known for early science fiction stories about the moon and sun</note>, a graceful play of fancy and satire; but we always find that at the bottom, the new world is only the one we ourselves live in. So strong is this tendency that even great natural (though non-initiated) Seers fall victim to it when untrained; witness Swedenborg <note>Emanuel Swedenborg (1688–1772), a scientist turned mystic who described travels to other planets in his visions</note>, who goes so far as to dress the inhabitants of Mercury, whom he meets in the spirit-world, in clothes such as are worn in Europe!

Commenting on this tendency, Flammarion says:

> It seems as if in the eyes of those authors who have written on this subject, the Earth were the model for the Universe, and the human of Earth, the model for the inhabitants of the Heavens. It is, on the contrary, much more probable that, since the nature of other planets is essentially varied, and the surroundings and conditions of existence essentially different—while the forces which preside over the creation of beings and the substances which enter into their mutual constitution are essentially distinct—it would follow that our mode of existence cannot be regarded as in any way applicable to other globes. Those who have written on this subject have allowed themselves to be dominated by terrestrial ideas, and have therefore fallen into error.†

# WORLDS MENTIONED IN THE "BIBLE."

But Flammarion <note>Camille Flammarion, the French astronomer previously mentioned</note> himself falls into the very error which he condemns here; he silently takes the conditions of life on Earth as the standard by which to determine how well other planets are adapted for habitation by "other human civilizations."

However, let us leave these useless and empty speculations. Though they seem to fill our hearts with a glow of enthusiasm and enlarge our mental and spiritual reach, they actually only cause a false sense of excitement. They blind us more and more to our ignorance—not only regarding the world we inhabit, but even the infinite depths contained within ourselves.

Therefore, when we find "other worlds" mentioned in the sacred scriptures of humanity, we may safely conclude that they refer not only to other states of our Planetary Chain <note>the series of seven globes through which life evolves in Theosophy</note> and Earth, but also to other inhabited globes—stars and planets. Furthermore, no actual speculations were ever made about the latter. All of antiquity believed in the Universality of Life. But no truly initiated seer of any civilized nation has ever taught that life on other stars could be judged by the standard of terrestrial life. What is generally meant by "Earths" and "Worlds" relates (*a*) to the "rebirths" of our globe after each <term>Manvantara</term> <note>original: "Manvantara"; a long period of cosmic activity in Hindu philosophy</note> and a long period of <term>Obscuration</term> <note>original: "Obscuration"; a period of rest or dormancy for a planet</note>; and (*b*) to the periodic and total changes of the Earth's surface, when continents disappear to make room for oceans, and oceans and seas are violently displaced and sent rolling to the poles to give up their places to new continents.

We may begin with the *Bible*—the youngest of the world's scriptures. In *Ecclesiastes*, we read these words of the King-Initiate <note>King Solomon, traditionally regarded in occultism as a high spiritual initiate</note>:

> One generation passes away and another generation comes, but the earth remains forever. . . . The thing that has been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done, is that which shall be done, and there is no new thing under the sun.*

Under these words, it is not easy to see the reference to the successive catastrophes by which the <term>Races</term> <note>in Theosophy, "Races" refers to the major evolutionary stages of humanity</note> of mankind are swept away, or, going further back, to the various transitions of the globe during its formation process. But if we are told that this refers only to *our world as we now see it*, then we shall refer the reader to the *New Testament*, where St. Paul speaks of the Son (the manifested Power) whom God has appointed heir of all things, "by whom also he made the worlds" (plural).† This "Power" is <term>Chokmah</term> <note>original: "Chokmah"; the Hebrew word for "Wisdom"</note>, the Wisdom and the Word.

-># THE SECRET DOCTRINE.<-

We will likely be told that by the term “worlds,” the stars, heavenly bodies, and so on, were meant. In his work (volume 1, page 309) treating the indefinite period of the six days—or shall we say the “too definite” period of the six days—of creation and the 6,000 years, he confesses that we are in total darkness as to the meaning of this statement by St. Paul. He says this is true unless we are permitted to suppose that it alludes to the period which elapsed between the *first* and *second* verses of chapter 1 of *Genesis*, and thus to those primitive revolutions—that is, the destructions and the reproductions of the world—indicated in chapter 1 of *Ecclesiastes*; or, to accept, as many others do in a *literal* sense, the passage in chapter 1 of *Hebrews* that speaks of the creation of “worlds” in the plural. It is very singular, he adds, that all the <term>cosmogonies</term> <note>theories regarding the origin of the universe</note> should agree in suggesting the same idea, and preserve the tradition of a first series of revolutions, because of which the world was destroyed and renewed again.

Thus, in four <term>meteorites</term> <note>rocks from space that fall to Earth</note> which fell respectively at Alais in France, the Cape of Good Hope, Hungary, and again in France, analysis found <term>graphite</term>, a form of <term>carbon</term> known to be invariably associated with organic life on our Earth. That the presence of this carbon is not due to any action occurring within our own atmosphere is shown by the fact that carbon has been found in the very center of a meteorite. Furthermore, in one which fell at Orgueil <note>original: Argueil</note>, in the south of France, in 1857, scientists found water and peat <note>original: turf</note>, the latter being always formed by the decomposition of vegetable substances.

And further, by examining the astronomical conditions of the other planets, it is easy to show that several are far better adapted for the development of life and intelligence—even under the conditions with which humans are acquainted—than our Earth is. For instance, on the planet Jupiter, the seasons, instead of varying between wide limits as they do here...

# WHAT FLAMMARION TELLS US.

Jupiter’s seasons change by almost imperceptible degrees and last twelve times longer than our own. Because of the tilt of its axis, Jupiter's seasons are caused almost entirely by the eccentricity <note>original: eccentricity; the degree to which an orbit deviates from a perfect circle</note> of its orbit, and therefore they change slowly and regularly. We are often told that no life is possible on Jupiter because it is in an incandescent <note>original: incandescent; glowing with intense heat, like a star</note> state. However, not all astronomers agree with this. For instance, our position is the same as that declared by Monsieur Flammarion <note>Camille Flammarion (1842–1925), a renowned French astronomer and prolific author who popularized the idea that other planets were inhabited</note>; and *he ought to know*.

On the other hand, Venus would be less suited for human life as it exists on Earth, since its seasons are more extreme and its changes in temperature are more sudden. It is curious, however, that the duration of a day is nearly the same on the four inner planets: Mercury, Venus, the Earth, and Mars.

On Mercury, the Sun’s heat and light are seven times greater than they are on the Earth, and astronomy teaches that it is enveloped in a very dense atmosphere. Since we see that life appears more active on Earth in proportion to the light and heat of the Sun, it would seem more than probable that the intensity of life is far, far greater on Mercury than it is here.

Venus, like Mercury, has a very dense atmosphere, as does Mars. The snows that cover their poles, the clouds that hide their surfaces, the geographical layout of their seas and continents, and the variations of their seasons and climates are all closely analogous—at least to the eye of the physical astronomer. But such facts, and the considerations they raise, refer only to the possibility of *human life as known on Earth* existing on these planets. That some forms of life similar to those we know are possible on these planets has long since been abundantly demonstrated. It seems perfectly useless to go into detailed questions regarding the physiology <note>the biological study of how living bodies function</note> of these hypothetical inhabitants, since, after all, the reader can only arrive at an imaginary extension of his own familiar surroundings. It is better to be content with the three conclusions formulated by Monsieur Flammarion, whom we have quoted so extensively, as rigorous and exact deductions from the *known facts and laws of science*:

i. The various forces that were active at the beginning of evolution gave birth to a great variety of beings on the several worlds, in both the organic and inorganic kingdoms.

ii. From the start, living beings were designed with forms and organisms that corresponded to the physiological state of each inhabited globe.

Finally, any reader who might be inclined to question the validity of these conclusions because they seem to contradict the *Bible* should consult an appendix in Monsieur Flammarion’s <note>Camille Flammarion (1842–1925), a renowned French astronomer and author</note> work, which deals with this question in detail. In a book such as this, it seems unnecessary to point out the logical absurdity of those clergy members who deny the plurality of worlds <note>plurality of worlds: the philosophical and scientific concept that many planets in the universe are inhabited by intelligent life</note> based solely on biblical authority.

In this regard, we might well recall the days when the intense zeal of the early Church opposed the idea that the Earth is round. They argued that nations living at the Antipodes <note>Antipodes: the parts of the earth directly opposite to each other; specifically, the idea of people living "upside down" on the other side of the globe</note> would be outside the reach of salvation. We may also remember how long it took for early Science to dismantle the idea of a solid firmament <note>firmament: the ancient concept of the sky as a solid dome or "vault" over the earth</note>, in the tracks of which the stars supposedly moved for the sole benefit of humanity on Earth.

The theory of the Earth's rotation was met with similar opposition—even leading to the martyrdom of its discoverers. This was because, besides stripping our world of its prestigious central position in space, the theory created an appalling confusion of ideas regarding the Ascension <note>Ascension: the Christian belief in Jesus’s physical departure from Earth into Heaven</note>. Since the terms "up" and "down" were proven to be merely relative, the question of the exact location of Heaven became quite complicated!*

According to the best modern calculations, there are no fewer than 500,000,000 stars of various sizes within the range of our best telescopes. As for the distances between them, they are beyond calculation. Is it possible, then, that our microscopic Earth—a "grain of sand on an infinite seashore"—is the only center of intelligent life? Our own Sun, which is itself 1,300,000 times larger than our planet, seems insignificant next to the giant star Sirius; and Sirius, in its turn, is dwarfed by other suns in the infinite reaches of space. The self-centered concept of Jehovah as the special guardian of a small and obscure semi-nomadic tribe is barely tolerable compared to the idea that sentient life exists only on our microscopic globe. The primary reasons for this narrow view were undoubtedly: (**a**) astronomical ignorance on the part of early Christians, combined with an inflated sense of man’s own importance—a crude form of selfishness; and (**b**) the fear that, if the hypothesis of millions...

> Long before the empires of China and India, there were nations that were cultured, learned, and powerful. A flood of barbarians overpowered them, throwing them back into their primitive state of ignorance and savagery—what is called the "state of pure nature."†

What was a clever guess for Voltaire’s great mind was a "question of historical facts" for Bailly. He wrote:

> I place great value <note>original: I make great case</note> on ancient traditions preserved through a long series of generations.

He believed it was possible that a *foreign* nation could, after instructing another nation, disappear so completely that it left no traces behind. When asked how it could have happened that this ancient—or rather, archaic—nation left no memory in the human mind, he answered that Time was a pitiless devourer of facts and events. ->### THE TOMBS OF THE GIANTS.<-

These monuments are twin sisters of those at Stonehenge. Such stone tables <term>original: "dolmens"; prehistoric structures consisting of a large flat stone laid on upright ones</term> and prehistoric monuments are found in almost every latitude. They are located in the Mediterranean basin; in Denmark (among the local burial mounds <term>original: "tumuli"</term> from twenty-seven to thirty-five feet high); in Shetland; in Sweden, where they are called *Ganggriften* <note>original: *Ganggriften*; Swedish for "passage graves"</note>; in Germany, where they are known as the giant tombs (*Hünengräben* <note>original: *Hünengräben*; German for "giants' graves"</note>); in Spain, where the Antiguera stone table is near Malaga; in Africa; in Palestine and Algeria; in Sardinia, with the *Nuraghi* <note>original: *Nuraghi*; ancient megalithic edifices in Sardinia</note> and the *Sepolture dei Giganti* <note>original: *Sepolture dei Giganti*; Italian for "Tombs of the Giants"</note>; in Malabar; in India, where they are called the tombs of the *Daityas* <note>original: *Daityas*; giants or titans in Hindu mythology</note> and of the *Râkshasas* <note>original: *Râkshasas*; man-eating demons or giants</note>, the "man-demons" of Lanka; in Russia and Siberia, where they are known as the *Kurgan* <note>original: "Koorgan"; burial mounds</note>; in Peru and Bolivia, where they are called *Chulpas* <note>original: "Chulpas" or "Chullpas"; ancient Aymara funerary towers</note> or burial places, and so on.

There is no country from which they are absent. Who built them? Why are they all connected with serpents and dragons, or with alligators and crocodiles? Because remains of "Paleolithic man" were, it is thought, found in some of them, and because bodies of later races were discovered in the burial mounds of America with the usual equipment of bone necklaces, weapons, and stone or copper urns, they are therefore considered ancient *tombs*! However, surely the two famous mounds—one in the Mississippi valley and the other in Ohio, known respectively as the "Alligator Mound" and the "Great Serpent Mound"—were never intended to be tombs.* Yet we are told authoritatively that these mounds, and the people who built them, are all "Pelasgic" <note>original: "Pelasgic"; referring to the Pelasgians, a term used by ancient Greeks for their predecessors</note> in Europe, occurring before the Incas in America, but not from "extremely distant times." Finally, the opinion of the German biologist Rudolf Virchow regarding the giant tombs of Germany is now accepted as a self-evident truth. That biologist says:

> The tombs alone are gigantic, and not the bones they contain.

> According to the statements of the later Parsi <note>original: "Parsî"</note> Scriptures, the *seven Karshvars are to be considered as completely disconnected parts of the earth* [which they surely are. For] *between them there flows the ocean, so that it is impossible, as stated in several passages, to pass from one Karshvar to another.*‡

The “Ocean” is *Space*, of course, for the latter was called “Waters of Space” before it was known as *Ether*. Moreover, the word Karshvar is consistently translated as <term>Dvîpa</term> <note>a Sanskrit term meaning "island" or "continent"</note>, and *Hvaniratha* <note>the central Karshvar inhabited by humans</note> is translated as *Jambudvîpa* <note>the name of the central continent in Hindu geography</note> (*Neryosangh*, the translator of the *Yasna*).§ But this fact is not taken into account by the Orientalists, and therefore we find even such a learned Zoroastrian and Parsi by birth as the translator of Dr. Geiger’s work, passing over without a word of comment various remarks of the former on the “incongruities” of this kind abounding in the Mazdean Scriptures. # THE DRUIDICAL BELIEF IN REBIRTH

Aelian <note>A Roman author and teacher</note> preserved an extract from Theophrastus written during the days of Alexander the Great. It is a dialogue between Midas the Phrygian and Silenus. Midas is told of a continent that had existed in ancient times that was so immense that Asia, Europe, and Africa seemed like poor islands compared to it. *It was the last to produce animals and plants of gigantic magnitudes. There, said Silenus, men grew to double the size of the tallest man in his (the narrator’s) time, and they lived until they were twice as old. They had wealthy cities with temples, and one such city held more than a million inhabitants; gold and silver were found there in great abundance.*

Grote’s suggestion that Atlantis was but a myth arising from a mirage—clouds on a dazzling sky taking the appearance of islands on a golden sea—is too insincere to be given further notice.

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

# A.

## SOME STATEMENTS IN THE CLASSICS ABOUT THE SACRED ISLANDS AND CONTINENTS, EXPLAINED ESOTERICALLY.

All that preceded this was known to Plato and to many others. But since no <term>Initiate</term> <note>Someone admitted into secret religious or philosophical knowledge</note> had the right to reveal and declare everything he knew, future generations received only hints. Because he aimed more to teach as a moralist than as a geographer, ethnologist, or historian, the Greek philosopher condensed the history of Atlantis—which spanned several million years—into a single event. He placed this event on one relatively small island measuring 3,000 stadia long by 2,000 wide (about 350 miles by 200, roughly the size of Ireland); in contrast, the priests spoke of Atlantis as a continent as vast as "all Asia and North Africa" combined.* <note>original: "Lybia"</note>

However altered in its general appearance, Plato’s narrative bears the mark of truth. It was not he who invented it, in any case, since Homer—who lived many centuries before him—also speaks in his *Odyssey* of the Atlantes (who are our Atlanteans) and of their island. Therefore, the tradition was older than the poet of Odysseus. The Atlantes and the Atlantides <note>The children of Atlas in Greek myth</note> of mythology are based upon the Atlantes and the Atlantides of history. Both Sanchuniathon <note>A legendary Phoenician author</note> and Diodorus <note>Diodorus Siculus, a Greek historian</note> have preserved the histories of those heroes and heroines, however much their accounts may have become mixed with mythical elements.

In our own day, we witness the extraordinary fact that the existence of such relatively recent figures as Shakespeare and William Tell is almost denied; attempts are made to show that one is a <term>pseudonym</term> <note>original: "nom de plume"</note> and the other a person who never existed. It is no wonder, then, that two powerful races—the Lemurians and the Atlanteans—have been merged over time and identified with a few semi-mythical peoples who all shared the same ancestral name.

If the Atlanteans never had their sleep disturbed by dreams, it is because that specific tradition refers to the earliest Atlanteans. # THE HEIRLOOM OF ATLANTIS.

Mount Atlas has been raised as a monument of the past. It is the only surviving, independent Western relic belonging to the continent on which the Third Race <note>The Lemurians, the predecessor to the Atlantean race in theosophical history</note> was born, developed, and fell.\* Australia is now considered part of the Eastern Continent. According to esoteric tradition, after "Proud Atlas" sank one-third of its size into the waters, its remaining two parts were left as a legacy of Atlantis.

This history was known to the priests of Egypt and to Plato himself. Only their solemn oath of secrecy—which extended even to the mysteries of Neo-Platonism—prevented the full truth from being revealed.† Indeed, knowledge of the last island of Atlantis was kept so secret because of the superhuman powers possessed by its inhabitants. They were thought to be the last direct descendants of the "Gods" or "Divine Kings." To reveal its location or its existence was a crime punishable by death. Theopompus says as much in his often-doubted work *Meropis*. He speaks of the Phoenicians as being the only sailors in the seas off the Western coast of Africa. They operated with such mystery that they often sank their own ships to ensure that inquisitive foreigners would lose all trace of them.

There are Orientalists and historians—who represent the majority—who remain unbothered by the blunt language of the Bible and some of the events narrated within it, yet show great disgust at the "immorality" found in the pantheons of India and Greece.‡ We are often told that ancient writers like Euripides, Pindar, and even Plato expressed the same disgust. They, too, felt irritated by the myths invented by others—"those miserable stories of the poets," as Euripides phrases it.§

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

But there may have been another reason for this, perhaps. To those who understood that there were multiple ways to interpret the symbolism of the gods' origins (<note>original: "Theogonic Symbolism"</note>), it seemed like a mistake to have expressed these truths in such crude and misleading language. An educated and learned philosopher could discern the "kernel of wisdom" beneath the "coarse rind" of the myth. He knew that the story concealed the great laws and truths of both psychic and physical nature, as well as the origin of all things. However, this was not the case for the uninitiated common person. To them, the literal meaning (<term>dead-letter</term>: the surface-level or literal reading of a text without regard for its deeper meaning) was religion itself, and any deeper interpretation was considered sacrilege. These literal stories could neither enlighten them nor make them better people, especially since the gods in these myths often set such poor examples. But to the philosopher—and especially to the Initiate—Hesiod’s *Theogony* is as historically accurate as any history can be. Plato accepted it as such and shared as much of its truth as his oaths of secrecy allowed.

The fact that the Atlanteans claimed Uranus as their first king, and that Plato begins his story of Atlantis with the division of the great continent by Neptune (the grandson of Uranus), shows that there were other continents before Atlantis and other kings before Uranus. For Neptune, whose lot it was to receive the great continent, finds only one human couple made of clay on a small island. This couple represents the first physical *human* man, whose origin began with the final sub-races of the Third Root-Race <note>The Lemurians</note>. The god marries their daughter, Clito, and it is his eldest son, Atlas, who receives the mountain and the continent that were named after him.*

Now, all the gods of Olympus, as well as the deities of the Hindu pantheon and the Rishis <note>Ancient sages or inspired poets</note>, were seven-fold personifications of: 
1. The **Noumena** (<term>Noumena</term>: the spiritual essence of a thing, as opposed to its physical appearance) of the Intelligent Powers of Nature; 
2. Cosmic Forces; 
3. Celestial Bodies; 
4. Gods or **Dhyân Chohans** (<note>theosophical term for "Lords of Light," high-ranking celestial beings</note>); 
5. Psychic and Spiritual Powers; 
6. Divine Kings on Earth, or the incarnations of the gods; 
7. Terrestrial Heroes or Men. 

The knowledge of how to distinguish which of these seven forms was intended has always belonged to the Initiates, whose earliest predecessors created this system of symbols and allegories.

Thus, while Uranus (or the group representing this celestial assembly) reigned and ruled over the Second Race and their continent, Cronus (or Saturn) governed the Lemurians. Meanwhile, Jupiter, Neptune,† and others were part of the allegory concerning Atlantis, which at that time represented the entire Earth.

# “THE GREATER GODS OF OLYMPOS.”

During the era of the Fourth Race, Poseidonis—the last island of Atlantis and the “third step” of Idas-pati <note>original: Idas-pati — a name for Vishnu meaning "Lord of the Earth"</note>, or Vishnu, in the mystic language of the Secret Books—lasted until about 12,000 years ago.\* The Atlanteans mentioned by the historian Diodorus Siculus were correct in claiming that their country, the region surrounding Mount Atlas, was where “the Gods were born”—meaning where they “incarnated.” However, it was only after their fourth incarnation that they became, for the first time, human kings and rulers.

Diodorus speaks of Uranus as the first king of Atlantis. In doing so, he confuses the continents, whether intentionally or otherwise; but as we have shown, Plato indirectly corrects this statement. Uranus was the first teacher of astronomy to men because he is one of the seven Dhyân Chohans <term>Dhyân Chohans</term> (Celestial beings or “Lords of Meditation” who oversee the evolution of the cosmos) of that Second Period or Race. Uranus fathered the Titans of the Third Race, and it is they, personified by Saturn-Cronus, who mutilated him. This is because the Titans were the ones who fell *into physical generation*. When “*creation by spiritual will was superseded by physical procreation*,” they no longer had any need for Uranus <note>Uranus represents the pure, celestial sky or spiritual source that preceded physical birth</note>.

# THE POWER OF NAMES.

...heads like iron bullets, while the world alone suffers from such controversies. One side strengthens the ranks of Materialism, and the other bolsters the blind Sectarianism of the "dead-letter" <note>Taking religious or philosophical texts literally while ignoring their deeper spiritual or symbolic meaning.</note>. Now we may return once more to our immediate subject.

Atlantis is frequently mentioned under different names, many of which are unknown to modern commentators. The *power of names* is significant and has been understood since the first humans were taught by the Divine Masters. Because Solon <note>An ancient Athenian statesman and poet; Plato claims Solon heard the story of Atlantis from Egyptian priests.</note> had studied this power, he translated the "Atlantean" names into names he devised himself. Regarding the continent of Atlantis, it is important to remember that the accounts from ancient Greek writers contain a mix of information. Some statements refer to the vast continent itself, while others describe only its last small remaining island, Poseidonis. It has become common to assume all these accounts refer only to that island, but this is clearly incorrect given the conflicting descriptions regarding its size and other features.

For example, in the *Critias*, Plato states that the plain surrounding the city was itself enclosed by mountain ranges. He describes the plain as smooth, level, and oblong, stretching north and south. It measured three thousand stadia <term>stadia</term> (Ancient Greek units of distance; one stadium is approximately 607 feet or 185 meters) in one direction and two thousand in the other. They surrounded this plain with an enormous canal or trench that was 101 feet deep, 606 feet wide, and 1,250 miles long.*

However, in other passages, the entire size of the *island* of Poseidonis is described as being roughly the same size as this "plain around the city." Clearly, one set of descriptions refers to the vast continent, while the other refers to its final remnant—the island mentioned by Plato.

Furthermore, the standing army of Atlantis is said to have been over a million men, with a navy of 1,200 ships and 240,000 sailors. Such figures are impossible for a small island state roughly the size of Ireland!

Greek allegories give Atlas (representing Atlantis) seven daughters—representing seven sub-races—whose names are Maia, Electra, Taygeta, Asterope, Merope, Alcyone, and Celæno. From an ethnological <note>Referring to the study of human races and their origins.</note> perspective, they are said to have married Gods and become the mothers of famous heroes and the founders of many nations and cities. In astronomy, these daughters of Atlas have become the *seven Pleiades* <note>A well-known star cluster in the constellation Taurus, often called the "Seven Sisters."</note>. In Occult Science, both are linked to the destinies of nations—destinies shaped by the events of their early history according to Karmic Law <note>The spiritual principle of cause and effect.</note>.

As for the Hyperboreans <note>A mythical people in Greek legend who lived in a land "beyond the North Wind," described as a sun-drenched paradise.</note>, these people were described by Solinus Polyhistor <note>A 3rd-century Roman geographer known for his collection of wonders.</note> in this way:

# ATLANTIS, NECESSARY TO ETHNOLOGY

In his book *Island Life*—a work largely devoted to the question of how animals are distributed across the globe—Mr. Starkie Gardiner writes:

By a process of reasoning supported by a large array of different kinds of facts, Mr. Wallace arrives at the conclusion that the distribution of life upon the land as we see it today has been accomplished without the help of major changes in the relative positions of continents and seas. Yet, if we accept his views, we must believe that Asia and Africa, Madagascar and Africa, New Zealand and Australia, and Europe and America were united at some period that is geologically recent, and that seas with a depth of 1,000 fathoms <note>A fathom is a unit of length equal to six feet, used chiefly in measuring the depth of water.</note> were once bridged over. However, he treats as "utterly baseless and entirely opposed to all the evidence at our command" the theory that temperate Europe and temperate America, or Australia and South America, have ever been connected except by way of the Arctic or Antarctic Circles, and that lands now separated by seas deeper than 1,000 fathoms were ever united.

It must be admitted that Mr. Wallace has succeeded in explaining the main features of how life is currently distributed without needing to bridge the Atlantic or Pacific Oceans, except toward the Poles. Yet, I cannot help thinking that some of the facts might be more easily explained by admitting the former existence of a connection between the coast of Chile and Polynesia, and between Great Britain and Florida—connections suggested by the undersea banks that stretch between them. Nothing has been proven that makes these direct connections impossible, and no physical reason has been offered as to why the ocean floor could not be pushed upward from any depth. The route by which the flora <note>The plant life of a particular region or period.</note> of South America and Australia are supposed to have mixed (according to the <term>Anti-Atlantean</term> and <term>Lemurian hypotheses</term> of Wallace) is blocked by almost insurmountable obstacles. Furthermore, the apparently sudden arrival of many subtropical American plants in our <term>Eocenes</term> <note>The Eocene is a geological epoch lasting from about 56 to 33.9 million years ago.</note> requires a connection further to the south than the current 1,000-fathom line. Geological forces are constantly active, and there is no reason why an *elevating force, once set in motion in the center of an ocean, should stop acting until a continent is formed*. These forces have acted in relatively recent geological time to lift the loftiest mountains on earth out of the sea. Mr. Wallace himself repeatedly admits that sea-beds have been elevated 1,000 fathoms and islands have risen from depths of 3,000 fathoms. To suppose that these uplifting forces are limited in power is, in my view, to again quote from *Island Life*, "utterly baseless and entirely opposed to all the evidence at our command."†

<margin>† Violent minor cataclysms <note>Sudden, violent geographic changes, like floods or volcanic eruptions.</note> and massive earthquakes are recorded in the records of most nations—if not all. The rising and sinking <note>original: "Elevation and subsidence"</note> of continents is always in progress. The entire coast of South America has been raised up 10 to 15 feet and settled down again in an hour. Huxley <note>Thomas Henry Huxley, a famous biologist and contemporary of Darwin.</note> has shown that the British Islands have been submerged beneath the ocean four times and subsequently raised again and populated. Within the last five or six thousand years, the shores of Sweden, Denmark, and Norway have risen from 200 to 600 feet; in Scotland, there are raised beaches with rocky islets <note>original: "outlying stacks and skerries"</note> standing above the shore that is now being worn away by the waves. The North of Europe is still rising from the sea, and South America shows the phenomenon of raised beaches over 1,000 miles long, now at a height varying from 100 to 1,300 feet above sea level. On the other hand, the coast of Greenland is sinking fast, so much so that the Greenlander will not build by the shore. All these phenomena are certain. Why then may a gradual change not have given way to a violent cataclysm in remote ages—such cataclysms occurring on a smaller scale even now, for example <note>original: "e.g."</note>, the case of Sunda Island with the destruction of 80,000 Malays?</margin>

The two interpreters are entirely in disagreement with one another. Lyell's solution is as follows. As a disbeliever in sudden catastrophic <note>original: "cataclysmal"</note> changes due to the absence (?) of any reliable historical data on the point, and because of a strong leaning toward the idea that geological changes happen gradually and uniformly <note>original: "uniformitarian"</note>,† he attempts to trace the Atlantis "tradition" to the following sources:

(1) Primitive tribes connect catastrophes with an avenging God, who is assumed to punish immoral races in this way.

(2) Therefore, the beginning of a new race is logically seen as a virtuous one.

(3) The primary source of the geological basis of the tradition was Asia—a continent subject to violent earthquakes. Exaggerated accounts would thus be handed down through the ages.

(4) Egypt, being herself free from earthquakes, nevertheless based her significant geological knowledge on these traditions of ancient catastrophes.

We have focused on the ancient records of nations and the doctrine of chronological and psychic cycles <term>original: "psychic cycles"; the idea that human consciousness and spiritual awareness evolve in predictable historical patterns</term>, for which these records are tangible proof. When dealing with the secret annals and traditions of so many nations—whose very origins have never been proven by anything more than theoretical guesses—and when presenting the beliefs and philosophy of races that lived before recorded history, it is not as easy to manage the subject matter as it would be if we were only concerned with the philosophy and evolution of one specific race.

The birth and evolution of the "Sacred Science of the Past" are lost in the very depths <note>original: "night of Time"</note> of time. They attribute these accounts to a lack of observation by ancient writers or to superstition born from the ignorance of antiquity. It is, therefore, impossible to treat this subject as one would the ordinary...

## HEAR BOTH SIDES.

The development of an art or science in any well-known historical nation follows a pattern. It is only by presenting the reader with an abundance of proof—all showing that in every age and under every level of civilization and knowledge, the educated classes of every nation echoed one identical system and its fundamental traditions—that they can see that so many streams of the same water must have started from a common source. What was this source? If "coming events cast their shadows before them," then past events must also leave an impression behind. It is, therefore, by these shadows of the ancient <note>original: "hoary"</note> past and their imaginative outlines reflected in every religion and philosophy, that we can—by comparing them as we go—finally trace the origin that produced them. There must be truth and fact in what every ancient people accepted and made the foundation of their religions and faith. Moreover, as Haliburton said:

> Hear one side, and you will be in the dark; hear both sides, and all will be clear. <note>Thomas Chandler Haliburton was a 19th-century judge and author known for his "Sam Slick" stories.</note>

Until now, the public has only had access to one side—or rather, the biased views of two completely opposite groups of men: those of Science and those of Theology. While their initial assumptions <note>original: *primâ facie* — Latin meaning "at first glance" or "on the face of it"</note> or respective premises differ widely, their final conclusions are the same. Now, our readers have an opportunity to hear the other side, to learn the defendants' justification, and the nature of our arguments.

If the public is left to its old opinions—namely, on one side, that <term>Occultism</term> <note>The study of hidden spiritual laws and the hidden nature of reality.</note>, Magic, and ancient legends are all the result of ignorance and superstition; and on the other, that everything outside the orthodox path is the work of the devil—what will be the result? In other words, if theosophical and mystical literature had not gained an audience over the last few years, this present work would have had a very poor chance of being considered impartially. It would have been proclaimed—and by many will still be proclaimed—a fairy tale woven out of obscure <note>original: "abstruse"</note> problems, floating in and based on thin air. It would be seen as built of soap bubbles, bursting at the slightest touch of serious reflection, with no foundation to stand upon. Even the ancient writers, often dismissed as "superstitious and gullible," have no clear or unmistakable references to it, and the symbols themselves fail to provide even a hint that such a system existed. Such would be everyone’s verdict. But when it becomes undeniably proven that the claim of the modern...
