# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

The claim of Asian nations to a Secret Science and a Hidden <note>original: "Esoteric"</note> History of the world is based on fact. Though it has been unknown to the masses until now and remains a hidden mystery even to the learned—because they have never had the key to correctly understand the many hints dropped by ancient classical writers—it is still no fairy tale, but a reality. If this is true, then the present work will become merely the first of many more such books. The statement that even the "keys" discovered by some great scholars have proven too "rusty" for use, and that they are only silent witnesses to the existence of mysteries behind the veil that cannot be reached without a new key, is supported by too many proofs to be easily dismissed. An example can be given from the history of Freemasonry as an illustration.

In his *Occult Masonry* <note>original: "Maçonnerie Occulte"</note>, Ragon—an illustrious and learned Belgian Mason—rightly or wrongly criticizes English Masons for having made Masonry too literal <note>original: "materialized"</note> and for dishonoring it. He argues that Masonry was once based upon the Ancient Mysteries, but that English Masons, due to a mistaken idea about the origin of their trade, adopted the names "Freemasonry" and "Freemasons." This mistake, he says, is due to those who connect Masonry with the *building of Solomon’s Temple*. He ridicules this idea, stating:

> The Frenchman knew well, when he adopted the title of Freemason, that it was not a matter of building even the smallest wall. Instead, having been initiated into the Mysteries hidden under the name of Freemasonry—which could only be the continuation or the renewal of the ancient Mysteries—he was to become a "Mason" in the same way as Apollo or Amphion <note>In Greek mythology, Apollo and Amphion were said to have built the walls of cities like Troy and Thebes using divine music rather than physical tools.</note>. And do we not know that when the ancient initiated poets spoke of the *foundation of a city*, they meant the establishment of a doctrine? Thus Neptune, the God of reasoning, and Apollo, the God of hidden things, presented themselves as masons before Laomedon, the father of Priam, to help him build the city of Troy—which is to say, to establish the Trojan religion.*

Such hidden sentences with double meanings are common in the works of ancient classical writers. Therefore, if an attempt were made to show that, for instance, Laomedon was the founder of a branch of Ancient <note>original: "Archaic"</note> Mysteries—in which the earth-bound material soul, the Fourth Principle <note>In theosophical terms, the "Fourth Principle" is Kama-rupa, the seat of animal desires and the emotional soul.</note>, was personified in Menelaus’ unfaithful wife, the beautiful Helen—and if Ragon had not come along to support what we asserted, we might have been told that no classical author mentions it. We would be told that Homer shows Laomedon building a *city*, not founding an *Inner Worship* <note>original: "Esoteric Worship"</note> or *Mysteries*. Who is left now, except for a few Initiates, who understands the language and the correct meaning of such symbolic terms?

But although we have pointed to many misunderstood symbols...

# THE PROLOGUE TO ESOTERIC TRUTH.

Regarding our thesis, more than one difficulty still remains to be overcome. The most significant among these obstacles is the issue of chronology <note>The arrangement of events in order of occurrence.</note>. However, this could hardly be avoided. Caught between theological timelines and those of the geologists—and further opposed by materialistic anthropologists who assign dates to humanity and nature that fit only their own theories—what could the author do except what she has done? 

Theology places the Great Flood <note>original: "Deluge"</note> in 2448 B.C. and the creation of the world only 5,890 years ago. Meanwhile, "exact" science—based on the accurate research of geologists and physicists—estimates the age of the Earth’s crust to be anywhere between ten million and one billion years (a *massive* difference, indeed!). To add to this, anthropologists, in their differing opinions on when humans first appeared, ask for anywhere between 25,000 and 500,000 years. Given this confusion, what can a student of the Secret Wisdom <note>original: "Occult Doctrine"</note> do but bravely present these hidden <note>original: "Esoteric"</note> calculations to the world?

To do this, it has been necessary to provide at least some "historical" proofs, even though we all know the true value of so-called "historical evidence." Whether humanity appeared on Earth 18,000 or 18,000,000 years ago makes no difference to secular <note>original: "profane"</note> history, since it only begins about two thousand years before our era. Even then, history grapples hopelessly with a clash of contradictory and self-destructive opinions. Nevertheless, out of respect for the average reader who has been raised to value "exact science," even that short history would remain meaningless unless the hidden teachings were supported on the spot—*whenever possible*—by references to historical names from a recognized historical period. 

This is the only guide that can be given to a beginner before they are permitted to start through the unfamiliar twists and turns of that dark labyrinth called the prehistoric ages. This necessity has been addressed. The author only hopes that the desire to provide ancient and modern evidence for a prehistoric past will not lead to accusations of being disorganized or jumbling together widely separated periods of history and tradition. Literary form and method had to be sacrificed for the sake of making the general explanation clearer.

To accomplish this task, the writer has used the unusual method of dividing each volume into three parts; the—

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE.

Only the first part of this work provides a sequential, though very fragmentary, history of the origin of the universe <note>original: "Cosmogony"</note> and the evolution of humanity on this globe. In discussing the origin of the universe and the subsequent development of mankind <note>original: "Anthropogenesis"</note>, it was necessary to show that no religion—from the very earliest times—has ever been based entirely on fiction. None was the object of a unique, "special revelation." Instead, it is rigid dogma alone that has always stifled original truth. Finally, no human-created doctrine or creed, no matter how sanctified by tradition and age, can compare in holiness to the religion of Nature.

The Key of Wisdom that unlocks the massive gates leading to the secret mysteries <note>original: "arcana"</note> of the innermost sanctuaries can only be found hidden in Nature's heart. This "heart" is located in the countries pointed to by the great visionary of the past century, Emanuel Swedenborg. There lies the Heart of Nature—the shrine from which the early races of original humanity emerged, and the cradle of *physical* man.

So far, we have provided the rough outlines of the beliefs and principles of the earliest ancient <note>original: "archaic"</note> races, as contained in their previously secret scriptural records. However, our explanations are by no means complete. They do not claim to present the full text, nor have they been interpreted using more than three or four "keys" out of the seven levels of hidden <note>original: "Esoteric"</note> interpretation. Even this has only been partially achieved. This work is too massive for any single person to undertake, let alone complete. Our main goal has been simply to prepare the ground.

We believe we have done this. These two volumes represent the work of a pioneer who has forced a way into the nearly impenetrable jungle of the "Land of the Occult." A beginning has been made in cutting down and uprooting the poisonous trees <note>original: "upas trees," referring to a Javanese tree legendary for its toxic effects on its surroundings</note> of superstition, prejudice, and arrogant ignorance. These two volumes should serve as a suitable introduction for the student to other works. 

Until the mental clutter of the ages is cleared from the minds of the Theosophists <note>Students of "Theosophy," a philosophy seeking knowledge of the divine through mystical insight and ancient wisdom</note> to whom these pages are dedicated, it is impossible for the more practical teachings in the Third Volume to be understood. Consequently, whether the final volume is ever published depends entirely on how Volumes I and II are received by Theosophists and seekers of hidden truth <note>original: "Mystics"</note>.
